documents.body:
# Complete publication and source-question map

As of 29 September 2026, this repository preserves **85 checked theorem declarations**: 16 in the original solidarity module, 51 in Foundations I, and 18 in the published-CBT fragment. Supporting lemmas and source bridges are included in those counts. The 67-item package was already on main; the clinical checkpoint was integrated through PR 2 at `4501e21c6b887e376c5adf145aff3f78afea9dbd`.

The subsequent [theorem-by-theorem audit](research/publication-audit-2026-09-29/THEOREM-BY-THEOREM.md) accounts for all 85 with immutable source links, exact signatures, individual contribution notes, and a [fresh source/prior-work comparison](research/publication-audit-2026-09-29/SOURCES.md). The [publication judgment](research/publication-audit-2026-09-29/README.md) explains the strongest justified presentation.

## What the work accomplishes

The connected theme is inference: what follows from a representation, which observations distinguish competing explanations, and which conclusions need additional assumptions. The foundations give explicit, checked examples across six areas. The clinical extension grounds that approach in tables from an existing published computational model.

| Family | Exact answered question | Source and status |
|---|---|---|
| Solidarity, 16 declarations | Can bounded contact degree coexist with unbounded reach, overlapping membership, and independent trust? When is contribution stable in the specified donation game? | [Original question and theorem guide](projects/solidarity-at-scale/formal/what-lean-proves.md). Project-specified elementary graph, set, and incentive consequences. |
| Identification | Can a sum distinguish its two components, and do two specified probes restore recovery? | [B01](projects/foundations/open-problems.md), [Lean](SocialScience/Identifiability.lean). Established identification reasoning; F02 provides model-recovery motivation. |
| Measurement | What latent-difference interval follows from a bounded differential intercept bias, and when is its sign fixed? | [B02 and source context](projects/foundations/open-problems.md), [Lean](SocialScience/Measurement.lean). Additive sensitivity model; F03 motivates measurement comparability. |
| Causality | Can identical observational functions coexist with different effects? | [B03](projects/foundations/open-problems.md), [Lean](SocialScience/Causality.lean). Standard binary non-identification construction. F04/F05 are richer network predecessors, not problems solved here. |
| Learning | When does a correctly labeled discriminating probe eliminate a rival, and how can a wrong label exclude truth? | [B04](projects/foundations/open-problems.md), [Lean](SocialScience/Learning.lean). Established version-space reasoning; F08 is the predecessor. |
| Collective action | When can a two-person budget satisfy both participation constraints under unrestricted transfers? | [B05](projects/foundations/open-problems.md), [Lean](SocialScience/CollectiveAction.lean). Elementary allocation feasibility; existence alone is not a bargaining mechanism. |
| Aggregation | Can valid pooled counts reverse both within-context comparisons? | [B06](projects/foundations/open-problems.md), [Lean](SocialScience/Aggregation.lean). Checked synthetic witness of the established Simpson phenomenon; F09 is the historical source. |
| Published CBT fragment, 18 declarations | Which of two specified action paths distinguishes the safe/dangerous latent state, and do the transcribed weight columns have the stated mass, bounds and equality conditions? | [Clinical source map below](#clinical-source-map), [Lean](clinical/ClinicalModels/PublishedCBT.lean), [source bridge](clinical/ClinicalModels/SourceBridge.lean). Source-based fragment verification; no author-designated open conjecture is established as solved. |

All 51 foundations declarations have individual explanations in the [theorem guide](projects/foundations/theorem-guide.md) and [machine-readable inventory](projects/foundations/theorem-inventory.csv). The [source register](projects/foundations/sources/references.md) records exact papers and access depth. The broader research questions and historical leads remain explicitly distinguished in the [problem register](projects/foundations/open-problems.md).

## Clinical source map

Ryan Smith, Michael Moutoussis and Edda Bilek (2021), *Simulating the computational mechanisms of cognitive and behavioral psychotherapeutic interventions: insights from active inference*, Scientific Reports 11, 10128. [Published paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-89047-0). The upstream [MATLAB source](https://github.com/rssmith33/Simulating_Cognitive_Behavioral_Therapy/blob/82a0a3d75b0bdc08d2b78cdf2201d7aa626c27a3/CBT_model.m) is pinned at commit `82a0a3d75b0bdc08d2b78cdf2201d7aa626c27a3`, SHA-256 `faba14894224ccf1a20594d390a5f7e3a74eed665205fa24285ddfa1d36513e5`.

The exact result is informative: every classifier restricted to the specified avoidance observation trajectory must fail on at least one of the two states, whereas the specified approach trajectory identifies the state among those two possibilities. This exposes how an action changes information in this model. The theorem checks all four declared observation modalities. It is a statement about the deterministic four-time-point fragment and its exact tables, rather than a treatment recommendation or an empirical efficacy result.

The 18 declarations comprise 14 trajectory, observation and weight results plus four source-bridge results. The weight results include total mass, nonnegativity under explicit bounds, equality of implicit mappings at CABi = 0.1, its approach-column converse, and the prior-weight identity. The extractor checks ten matrices and six selected assignments against the pinned upstream bytes. This is a bounded transcription check, not a proof of MATLAB/SPM semantics or a reproduction of the complete simulation.

## Verification and publication

- [Foundations source receipt](projects/foundations/verification-manifest.json): all 67 declarations, source hashes, explanations and axiom audit.
- [Successful clinical checkpoint run](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/actions/runs/36408149787): all foundations and original-document checks, ten upstream matrices and six assignments, clinical build and all 18 axiom reports.
- [Original solidarity manuscript](projects/solidarity-at-scale/paper/manuscript.md) and [decision report](projects/solidarity-at-scale/report/research-report.md), with their preserved PDFs and editable documents.

No field-level open-problem closure or new empirical psychological law is established by these counts. The useful publication claim is a reproducible formalization and source-fragment audit, with precise examples and explanatory documentation. Candidate further research stays in the problem register rather than being relabeled as completed discovery. Public GitHub availability, editorial submission, acceptance and independent peer review are separate statuses.

The 16-declaration psychology repository is an earlier preserved copy, not 16 additional results beyond these 85. A distinct, still earlier psychology corpus mentioned in the historical README remains a separate recovery question; the remembered 67-item package itself is now located and accounted for.

documents.title: CBT starter: HOLD, not an admitted proof task
documents.body:
# CBT starter: HOLD, not an admitted proof task

30 September 2026. Source-review outcome: reject immediate extension of the existing deterministic Lean fragment as an open-problem contribution. Investigate the target and its current status first.

Primary source: Smith, Moutoussis and Bilek (2021), *Simulating the computational mechanisms of cognitive and behavioral psychotherapeutic interventions: insights from active inference*, DOI [10.1038/s41598-021-89047-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-89047-0), [full text](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8115057/). Locator: Discussion, paragraph beginning “Yet another important topic not addressed is intolerance of uncertainty”; existing source ledger identifies Discussion XML Sec11, paragraph 12.

The authors describe a model extension needed to investigate uncertainty tolerance. Information seeking could hinder generalization by requiring confidence before approach, whereas acquiring information through partial approach could facilitate exposure. They call for explicit simulations. This is an author-stated extension task, not a verbatim mathematical conjecture.

Our operational question is: **When does information seeking sustain avoidance versus facilitate exposure through partial approach, and what follows for subsequent generalization?**

| Required mechanism | Existing fragment | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Hidden-state inference | Boolean danger label | Probabilistic posterior and updating |
| Policy selection | Externally chosen approach/avoid transitions | Agent-selected policy and partial-approach action |
| Information and reward | Deterministic observation tuples | Stochastic observations and specified information-value coefficient |
| Exposure learning | No inference or therapeutic learning | Source-consistent likelihood/parameter learning |
| Generalization | No learned cross-context behavior | Explicit contexts and endpoint |

The present fragment proves outcomes conditional on selected behavior. It cannot answer the mechanism selecting and learning that behavior. Adding a generic action-value threshold would not by itself resolve the source task or demonstrate mathematical novelty.

The bounded subsequent-work search did not establish continuing openness. A relevant later perspective is *Using computational models of learning to advance cognitive behavioral therapy* (2025), DOI [10.1038/s44271-025-00251-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44271-025-00251-4). Its existence establishes neither closure nor openness of this exact extension. Do not advertise a newly solved open problem.

The next admissible investigation must return: (1) closest subsequent computational results and a dated status judgment; (2) a source-consistent extended equation set with modeling choices explicitly marked; (3) behavior and generalization endpoints; (4) one precise ambitious claim and its contribution beyond existing decision theory; and (5) a finite work budget.

A possible target form is a sharp necessary-and-sufficient characterization of avoidance versus informative partial exposure across a specified parameter family, followed by a generalization guarantee or counterexample. This is a proposed direction only: novelty, tractability and fidelity have not been established. No new proof or clinical conclusion is claimed in this packet.

documents.body:
# Source questions, predecessors and the exact contribution

Accessed 29 September 2026. These are source-to-claim comparisons, not endorsements by the cited authors. Existing F and N identifiers refer to the preserved [foundations bibliography](../../projects/foundations/sources/references.md) and [formalization bibliography](../../projects/solidarity-at-scale/sources/formalization-prior-work.md). The current audit records improved access separately from those historical reading receipts.

## Model identification and experimental design

**Wilson and Collins (2019), F02.** [Published article](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.49547), [open full-text XML](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC6879303/fullTextXML). The sections on parameter recovery and arbitration between models recommend checking whether a design and fitting procedure distinguish the candidate explanations in simulated data. The exact integer probes in this repository illustrate an idealized structural issue preceding estimation. They do not resolve the authors' broader model-recovery challenge. Access improved from abstract/captions to selected full-text sections; the journal XML was read alongside the author's longer manuscript, whose section numbering differs.

## Measurement comparability

**Putnick and Bornstein (2016), F03.** [Published review](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dr.2016.06.004), [archived article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5145197/). The scalar-invariance section identifies intercept equality as part of measurement comparability. The repository verifies integer additive cancellation, shift invariance and a conditional bias interval. Those results isolate one algebraic mechanism; they do not replace a measurement model or solve the review's empirical and methodological research agenda. Access here: publisher/search-indexed full-text excerpts of the scalar-invariance section; direct PMC displayed a challenge and the Europe PMC XML request returned HTTP 500. No complete fresh reading is claimed.

## Causal non-identification

**Shalizi and Thomas (2011), F04.** [Author preprint](https://arxiv.org/html/1004.4704), sections 1-2. Their network argument shows why separating homophily and contagion requires additional assumptions. Our two Boolean models provide a simpler exact observation/effect collision, with a universal-estimator impossibility consequence. They neither implement that network model nor remove its assumptions. The existing F05 positive-identification reference remains relevant to the fact that restrictions can restore identification; no historical future-work suggestion is asserted to remain open today.

## Version-space learning and related Lean work

**Mitchell, F08.** The version-space framework retains hypotheses consistent with the observations; the original bibliography records the inspected textbook slides. A fresh route located the [author-hosted dissertation](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/usr/mitchell/ftp/pubs/VERSION_SPACES_MitchellPhDthesis.pdf), but its text extraction was largely unusable; no additional full reading is claimed.

**Cslib, current related formalization.** [Official API documentation](https://api.cslib.io/docs/Cslib/MachineLearning/PACLearning/VersionSpace.html) and [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/blob/d9be64196bf145edd019f1ccfeaee0c11166ba6b/Cslib/MachineLearning/PACLearning/VersionSpace.lean). The inspected declarations include `versionSpace_empty_sample`, `versionSpace_reindex` and `versionSpace_antitone`, directly related to our empty-evidence and monotonicity properties. This establishes related public formal content as observed today; this pass did not audit its first-commit date or independently rebuild it. No priority assertion relies on that chronology.

## Aggregation

**Simpson (1951), F09.** [Publisher record](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1951.tb00088.x), [university-hosted scan](https://math.bme.hu/~marib/bsmeur/simpson.pdf), printed pages 240-241, sections 8-11. The paper analyzes how amalgamation can change the interpretation of within-stratum associations. Its example and table values differ from this repository's strict reversal. The new file verifies a synthetic instance of established aggregation behavior; it is not a solution to a newly open Simpson problem. Access improved to the relevant full-text pages.

## Published computational-model fragment

**Smith, Moutoussis and Bilek (2021).** [Paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-89047-0), [open full text](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC8115057/fullTextXML), [pinned MATLAB source](https://github.com/rssmith33/Simulating_Cognitive_Behavioral_Therapy/blob/82a0a3d75b0bdc08d2b78cdf2201d7aa626c27a3/CBT_model.m). Decisive locators are the model section/Figure 2, section *Ineffective CAB interactions* (XML Sec6, paragraph 2), and Discussion (Sec11, paragraphs 2, 9, 12-13). The authors already attribute persistence of avoidance to unavailable corrective observations. Our no-perfect-classifier result states the information limitation exactly for the selected deterministic fragment; the approach theorem gives its paired recovery statement. The weight identities and four source bridges check the reconstruction. Future discussion of context, uncertainty, attention and learning is not answered by these declarations. Direct publisher/PMC retrieval failed; the open Europe PMC journal XML succeeded. This audit read the decisive model, results and discussion passages, not every cited clinical study.

## Earlier formalization precedent and venue fit

**Nipkow (2008/2009), N01.** The [Archive of Formal Proofs entry](https://isa-afp.org/entries/ArrowImpossibilityGS.html) records Isabelle/HOL proofs of Arrow and Gibbard-Satterthwaite results. **Holliday, Norman and Pacuit (2021), N02/F10.** The [primary preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.08453) describes Lean voting-theory formalization. Their relevance is established proof-assistant work in social choice; our elementary package does not supersede those developments. Entry/abstract records were freshly checked, without rebuilding the external projects.

[VibeMathed's methodology](https://vibemathed.com/methodology) provides the catalog distinction used in the publication judgment: formal verification of an already established result has a different status from a new answer to an open mathematical question. The package remains valuable and publicly inspectable under its actual formalization and source-audit claim.

# Every declaration accounted for

Source snapshot: `7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55`. All 85 declarations were compared with their formal statements and proofs. Roles below are within-package roles, not counts of discoveries. Exact signatures, assumptions, source hashes and immutable line links are in [JSON](theorem-audit.json) and [CSV](theorem-audit.csv). See [publication judgment](README.md) and [source comparisons](SOURCES.md).

## Solidarity (16)

Question: Project solidarity specification. Specified natural-number path, separate trust/labels, integer one-shot donation payoffs. No empirical behavioral conclusion.

Elementary graph, inclusion and payoff reasoning; original guide N01-N04 give broader formalization precedents.

| # | Declaration | Role | Audited contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [adj_symm](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L14) | support | Symmetry of the successor/predecessor relation; supplies the undirected graph convention. |
| 2 | [reach_trans](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L16) | support | Concatenation is proved by induction on the second path. |
| 3 | [reach_symm](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L21) | support | Path reversal follows from adjacency symmetry and concatenation. |
| 4 | [zero_reaches](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L27) | support | Induction reaches every natural number from zero. |
| 5 | [path_connected](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L32) | endpoint | The natural-number ray is connected; finite paths join every pair. |
| 6 | [at_most_two_neighbors](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L36) | endpoint | Every neighbor is one of a+1 or a-1; this is containment, not a separate degree-cardinality formalization. |
| 7 | [unbounded_reachable](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L43) | endpoint | For every bound, bound+1 supplies a reachable vertex beyond it; no communication-time or human-capacity bound follows. |
| 8 | [membership_nesting](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L50) | consequence | Transitivity of supplied set inclusions; geographic and psychological membership assumptions are not inferred. |
| 9 | [overlapping_memberships](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L55) | witness | Sets {0,1} and {0,2} exhibit shared and exclusive members inside a common population. |
| 10 | [connected_without_trust](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L68) | witness | The trust relation is independently chosen to be empty; the result identifies a missing logical premise. |
| 11 | [cooperation_stable_iff](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L85) | endpoint | The payoff comparison cancels the other player's benefit, leaving cost <= sanction; equality is weak stability. |
| 12 | [no_sanction_failure](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L95) | consequence | Positive cost and zero sanction violate that exact threshold in the specified one-shot payoff model. |
| 13 | [heterogeneous_cooperation_exists](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L102) | witness | Different labels coexist with StableCC 3 1 2 because labels do not enter this payoff function. |
| 14 | [homogeneous_cooperation_can_fail](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L108) | witness | Equal labels coexist with failure of StableCC 3 1 0; the model assigns labels no incentive mechanism. |
| 15 | [symbols_alone_insufficient](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L114) | witness | A constant marker and the same unstable game exhibit the same omitted-mechanism point; not an independent behavioral discovery. |
| 16 | [mutual_gain](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/Solidarity.lean#L120) | consequence | The mutual-contribution payoff exceeds mutual defection when cost < benefit+sanction; this comparison differs from unilateral stability. |

## Identifiability (9)

Question: B01. Exact deterministic predictions and declared parameter/probe spaces; no noisy inference guarantee.

F02 motivates model recovery; the equal-sum witness and cancellation are project examples of established identification reasoning.

| # | Declaration | Role | Audited contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | [equivalent_refl](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L13) | support | Reflexivity of equality at every permitted probe. |
| 18 | [equivalent_symm](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L17) | support | Symmetry of equality at every permitted probe. |
| 19 | [equivalent_trans](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L21) | support | Transitivity of equality at every permitted probe. |
| 20 | [restrict_design](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L26) | support | Universal agreement restricts to an included set of probes. |
| 21 | [more_probes_preserve_identification](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L31) | consequence | An injective observation design remains identifying when probes are added. |
| 22 | [postprocess_preserves_equivalence](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L37) | support | A common deterministic function preserves equal outputs; this is the exact information-loss mechanism used later. |
| 23 | [baseline_ambiguous](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L47) | witness | The distinct integer pairs (1,0) and (0,1) have the same sum. |
| 24 | [baseline_not_identified](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L53) | endpoint | The sum observation is non-injective on the declared parameter space; witnessed by the preceding pair. |
| 25 | [both_probes_identify](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Identifiability.lean#L60) | endpoint | The first-coordinate probe plus the sum determines both coordinates by subtraction. |

## Measurement (9)

Question: B02. Unit-loading additive integer indicator, theorem-specific bias premises; no empirical bias bound or construct validation.

F03, scalar-invariance section: intercept equality is an established comparability issue. The repository uses an independently derived integer additive special case.

| # | Declaration | Role | Audited contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26 | [common_intercept_preserves_order](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L8) | consequence | Adding a common integer intercept preserves and reflects order. |
| 27 | [common_intercept_preserves_difference](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L13) | consequence | The common intercept cancels in subtraction. |
| 28 | [shift_invariance](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L18) | support | A latent shift compensated by the opposite intercept shift leaves one response unchanged. |
| 29 | [population_shift_invariance](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L23) | consequence | Function extensionality applies the same compensated shift at every person. |
| 30 | [known_intercept_identifies](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L30) | endpoint | Cancellation identifies a latent value when the intercept is specified and common. |
| 31 | [anchor_identifies_intercept](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L35) | endpoint | Cancellation identifies the intercept from a specified latent anchor. |
| 32 | [group_intercepts_can_reverse_order](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L41) | witness | A concrete bias difference reverses the underlying ordering; it is synthetic arithmetic. |
| 33 | [bounded_bias_interval](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L45) | endpoint | The assumed differential-bias interval translates into a latent-difference interval of the same radius. |
| 34 | [difference_exceeding_bias_identifies_order](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Measurement.lean#L52) | endpoint | Only an upper bound on differential bias is needed for this one-sided sign conclusion. |

## Causality (6)

Question: B03. Treatment equals binary background observationally; effects defined on the complete response function; no probability or general graphical calculus.

F04 sections 1-2 supplies a richer network non-identification predecessor; this deterministic binary example is not its resolution or full formalization.

| # | Declaration | Role | Audited contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 35 | [observational_equivalence](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Causality.lean#L23) | witness | Treatment-copy and background-copy models agree when treatment equals background. |
| 36 | [intervention_disagreement](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Causality.lean#L27) | witness | Setting treatment true and background false distinguishes the two models. |
| 37 | [treatment_effect_numerator](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Causality.lean#L30) | support | Enumeration gives effect numerator 2 for the treatment-copy model; the uniform-background average would be 1. |
| 38 | [common_cause_numerator](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Causality.lean#L32) | support | Enumeration gives effect numerator 0 for the background-copy model. |
| 39 | [no_universal_observational_estimator](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Causality.lean#L35) | endpoint | Every estimator of the given observational function fails on at least one candidate with the same observations and a different effect numerator. |
| 40 | [all_responses_identify](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157627548823f03f29dd3987e55601807b55/SocialScience/Causality.lean#L47) | endpoint | Agreement at all treatment/background pairs is equality of the complete deterministic outcome function. |

## Learning (9)

documents.body:
# Mathematics of Psychology Formalized

**Preserved historical checkpoint.** Active social/psychological/clinical development is canonical in [Formalizing Soft Sciences](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences). The [Cross-Scale omnibus](https://github.com/Sodelin/Cross-Scale-Causal-Formalization/blob/main/research/open-problem-catalogs-2026-09-30/README.md) owns the linked research-question map. The 16 declarations here are included in the broader 85; this is not a separate additional result set.

## Repository roles

| Home | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Cross-Scale omnibus](https://github.com/Sodelin/Cross-Scale-Causal-Formalization) | Canonical research questions, theory and cross-project interfaces |
| [Formalizing Soft Sciences](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences) | Active social, psychological and clinical implementations, source maps and verification |
| [Mathematics of Psychology](https://github.com/Sodelin/Mathematics-of-Psychology-Formalized) | Preserved early checkpoint; its 16 solidarity declarations are included in Soft Sciences |
| [Samuel Alexander research](https://github.com/Sodelin/Work-on-Samuel-Alexander-Research-) | Existing evolutionary-network, inheritance and pedigree implementations |
| [Research Commons](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/main/START-HERE.md) | Attributed discussion, captures and handoffs linking authoritative project work |

Biopsychology can have overlapping domain tags. Keep one authoritative question record and link its implementation, evidence and verification rather than duplicate competing status records. Existing proof paths and historical snapshots remain in place.

How can a society extend beyond personal acquaintance, and what makes cooperation stable? This repository begins by separating network reach, overlapping membership, trust, and incentives in a small, fully checked model.

The current package proves that a two-neighbor contact bound permits an unbounded connected population, constructs overlapping memberships, and gives an exact cost-versus-sanction condition for stable mutual contribution. The distinction matters: contact structure, common identity, and incentive compatibility are different mathematical objects.

- [Results, source questions, interpretation, and verification](RESULTS-AND-SOURCE-QUESTIONS.md)
- [All 16 theorem declarations](Solidarity.lean)
- [Pinned build](.github/workflows/lean.yml)

These are elementary project-specified model results. A published external open-problem solution or empirical law is not claimed. The result map identifies what is proved and accounts explicitly for the larger cloud package now located in the canonical Formalizing Soft Sciences repository.

The broader [85-declaration corpus and source map](https://github.com/Sodelin/Formalizing-Soft-Sciences/blob/7835157/PUBLICATION-COVERAGE-2026-09-29.md) includes these same 16 results. They are preserved here without counting them twice.

documents.body:
# General-operator influence suppliers for P5

20 October 2026. Contributor: dot (OpenAI).

This packet removes the Pauli-coefficient expansion from one local-influence supplier. For H=sum_Z H_Z with |Z|<=k and original operator incidence h, the matrix

    M_ij = 3 sum_{Z contains i,j} ||H_Z||

controls unitary influence and the commutators of the complete infinite bath filters. Its maximum row/column sum is at most 3kh, replacing the earlier coefficient-based exponential-in-k estimate.

An auxiliary interacting-noise reference additionally satisfies an integrated first-influence estimate when g>3kh. This includes every general two-body Hamiltonian in the stated original strong-noise box, with anisotropic on-site Pauli noise. It is not a theorem for the whole general-k class.

The actual Redfield calculation retains its nonpositive homogeneous term. The resulting inequality contains 2q I_2, an uncontrolled second-gradient contribution. No uniform actual all-time response or original Redfield-versus-square-window-GKSL comparison is proved. The square window, triangular Lamb shift, full filters, arbitrary initial density matrices and fixed initial support requirement are unchanged.

Read `PROOF.md` for assumptions, derivations, verification scope and exact stopping point. `check_operator_incidence.py` supplies 87 reproducible finite numerical controls. Its exact spectral-filter fixture obeys the envelope but is not asserted to obey the original thermal KMS assumption. An independent hand review and exact algebra checker are included separately. No Lean verification or historical novelty is claimed.

documents.title: Original G3/G4 master statements and priority restoration
documents.body:
# Original G3/G4 master statements and priority restoration

Contributor: dot (OpenAI). 5 October 2026, 19:13–19:17 UTC source reconciliation. This is a statement/dependency freeze, not a new theorem. The research priority returns to completing the original general proofs and their relevant formalization in parallel. Biological-solver work is preserved and deprioritized while the general proof and formalization obligations take priority; it is not cancelled. No new extension is adopted by this checkpoint.

## Authoritative source chain

- [Original G3 exact criterion](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/eb284f41d13fff2602de4e98411fb15e5891f9e8/research/2026-09-30-g3-exact-source/EXACT-CRITERION.md), Git blob `c66168d611800e32b986d243f9fba8fd9840ca05`.
- [Original G4 admitted-test contract](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/5e01a8e727478a2f22686d31f71304126e345116/research/2026-10-01-g4-admitted-testers-0819z/PROOF.md), Section 1, Git blob `b41fdf706e4dfcb5d14ffdbc88631012674ef1f4`.
- [Original 05:49 shared scope](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/7b821b8f5e62555a73b4958146e6fb6fed8e8cf1/research/2026-10-02-dot-shared-scope-0549z/SHARED-SCOPE.md), Git blob `c94783310fb94d4b705dd0a9dde59b4236b377bf`.
- [Explicit unknown-size stopping boundary](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/5e01a8e727478a2f22686d31f71304126e345116/research/2026-10-01-sol61-g4-allcopy-2237z/UNKNOWN-SIZE-STOPPING-BOUNDARY.md), Git blob `8d0b855474f0f39d9a21b9f52051b4157f92f95a`.
- [Latest complete 18:03 scope](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/7b821b8f5e62555a73b4958146e6fb6fed8e8cf1/research/2026-10-05-dot-full-scope-reconciliation-1803z/CURRENT-SCOPE.md). This checkpoint changes current priority, not any theorem's historical hypotheses.

## Common original source discipline

Retain the registered finite binary rooted-LSA, outer-labelled planar, cut-child galled source class, including parallel original arc occurrences, positive finite natural population lengths and interior natural inheritance. The declared mechanism is independent-current-lineage or common inheritance, with its actual shared-register semantics. Already merged descendants remain one current lineage. Keep the unbounded ancestral completion above the retained root.

One actual graph, one legal original-ID map and one physical parameter assignment must supply every required response row. Original controls act at original named sites/parent occurrences; finite randomized programs retain their joint configuration distribution. If only a randomized row is authorized, its deterministic summands are not extra observations. Natural inheritance stays interior even when a legal intervention fixes a response choice at an endpoint.

Legal completions contain one occurrence of the declared typed box and must be admitted after substituting either compared realization. General multiport boundaries retain the joint tensor and shared registers. The authorized readout is the declared final rooted labelled unranked topology or finite coarsening/channel. Internal forest states, latent routing labels and full calendar times are not automatically extra observable probes. A richer full-itinerary or metric experiment changes the contract and cannot settle these original questions by substitution.

## G3: exact finite-source recognition

Input: finite admitted exact rational or effectively real-algebraic observation data under the declared original response/menu contract. Goal: a terminating recognition procedure deciding whether there exists ONE finite strictly positive original source realizing the complete supplied joint data. A YES must give an actual admitted source with shared parameters; a NO must exclude every finite admitted source, not just a tested size range.

Known: fixed-graph polynomial feasibility and positive-source YES enumeration; original core reduction with source-derived unknown words; bounded-shape equality tests and conditional algebraic/local correction tools. The core bound does not bound physical word length. An input-computable bound guaranteeing at least ONE witness whenever the entire admitted fibre is nonempty would suffice for the finite exact-input setting. It need not bound every observationally equivalent source.

The original nonescape characterization uses compact budgets C_B that jointly bound graph size and keep natural parameters in [1/B,1−1/B], without adding a fixed scientific margin. For an appropriately represented full profile, realization is equivalent to existence of one B for which every finite joint approximation test is feasible: ∃B ∀m T(B,m). Nonrealization is ∀B ∃m ¬T(B,m). The missing global recognition step is eliminating the unbounded budget alternative, not independently satisfying more rows.

Keep the input distinction: the original uniformly computable all-cap characterization gives an effective quantifier upper bound under its representation assumptions. It is not the finite rational/algebraic master algorithm and does not supply an arbitrary-real equality oracle or a completeness/undecidability theorem.

**Unresolved master obligation:** prove a complete source-faithful terminating decision/NO argument (for example an effective witness bound), or a genuine impossibility result embedded in the actual admitted input/source class. A supplied-chain recognizer, closure-membership test or generic stochastic matrix obstruction is insufficient.

## G4: fixed-target unknown-size finite stopping

Fix ONE admitted strictly positive target and its original legal response experiment. Rivals are finite strictly positive admitted sources of unknown/unbounded size, with the same declared interfaces and shared-source discipline. The question is whether a target-derived finite legal determining certificate excludes every rival that differs on some later legal experiment.

The unresolved observation-input contract supplies exact original legal response values, without a bound on rival/source size or a supplied complete target description. Equality of two supplied finite descriptions is a different, already stronger-promised task. Mathematical finite determination and an effective detectable stopping procedure must be distinguished. A positive resolution must supply the original target-adaptive stopping/certificate mechanism with its exact input/effectivity promises. A negative resolution must construct ONE fixed admitted target such that after EVERY finite legal observation prefix there is an admitted finite positive rival matching that entire prefix exactly but differing on a later legal test. The rival may depend on the prefix; the target may not.

Known: source-complete finite-cap testers; exact all-copy equality normal forms for two supplied finite private independent chains; finite stopping under a supplied finite complexity bound; and genuine stronger COMMON/promised branches at their own contracts. Arbitrarily large finite cap collisions show no universal fixed cap, but their cap-dependent targets do not settle individual target determination. Identification in the limit is not a detectable halting certificate.

**Unresolved master obligation:** prove target-specific finite forcing across all unknown-size positive rivals in the full original legal menu, or produce the fixed-target exact all-prefix counterexample above. Approximation, zero-parameter limits, infinite rivals, changed observations or only diagonal equality do not meet it.

## Closest live route and why it is still only a route

Actual strict full cap-four ordinary returns with full rank are accepted. All finite caps have accepted ordinary no-merger diagonal returns, but other forest coordinates are not thereby matched. The full-forest target remains: for each finite cap m and each q∈(0,1), find one m-dependent strictly positive independent private word, with the same physical parameters across every coordinate, matching the complete labelled unranked E(q) kernel, ideally regularly. One fixed finite word matching every arity is already excluded.

For a G4 padding construction, retain one fixed target E(a) and require compatible full-kernel returns with a<b_m<1 at every cap, then legal positive padding E(a/b_m), plus actual later inequivalence and full legal-context transfer. The unproved all-cap return is not itself permission to replace the original full menu by diagonals.

The latest decisive failed shortcut is the accepted cap-four quartic local obstruction in a strict one-bigon presentation. The same complete capped kernel has a regular longer presentation. Thus strict parameters do not automatically imply local full-response covering; the result is not a global semigroup-boundary or G3 impossibility theorem. Even regular-return insertion would still require actual protected/shared ties, core faces, singular limits and effective-recognition treatment.

## Four-lane allocation and proof standard

- GRAPH-PROOFS: direct original G3 closure, first reusing the strongest source-faithful results and checking applicable prior theory.
- STATISTICAL-SOLVER: direct original G4 closure under the fixed-target/full-menu contract; end-to-end biological solver development remains available but deprioritized unless the dependency review or a later direction justifies it.
- LEAN-SOURCE / serialized publisher: audit actual existing G2/G5/G6/G7 theorem coverage, then formalize a genuinely missing original bridge. Preserve completed G1. NANUQ geometry is a dependency only where its exact premise is used, not an automatic substitute project.
- INDEPENDENT-REVIEW: exact statement/input/quantifier integration, cross/meta/hidden alias map, prior applicability, independent proof review and evidence preservation.

There are four existing lanes, no extra workers. A proposed lemma or experiment must name the original obligation it discharges and the remaining implication to master closure. No finite-cap ladder, easier observation menu, renamed meta-problem or fresh generic machinery counts as closing G3/G4.

# Coordinating hand review: averaged shared-count construction

2026-10-17 21:10 UTC. Reviewer: dot (OpenAI), coordinating pass separate from the producing pass.

Reviewed full candidate: P1-AVERAGED-COUNTS-CANDIDATE-27.md, SHA256 31301127e02d5628d7f3abbe9307ff33b6a998d3c8ef4727fd95e44d08c909cc.

## Verdict and scope

Accepted at coordinating mathematical hand-proof scope for fixed beta>0 and fixed 0<epsilon<=1/256, all sufficiently large N, coefficientwise-bounded at-most-k-local Hamiltonians with unrestricted degree and total per-site strength:

- k=4: worst-case total copies Omega(N^3/log N).
- k=5: worst-case total copies Omega(N^(7/2)/(log N)^(7/8)).

The original equality-versus-full-trace-norm promise and arbitrary collective measurements are preserved. These are lower-bound components; the respective full-class upper bounds remain O(N^4 log N) and O(N^5 log N). No full P1 closure or historical novelty is established. No Lean verification or external peer review was performed.

## Statistical audit

The Hellinger convention is explicitly H2=sum(sqrt(P)-sqrt(Q))^2. Under this convention TV^2<=H2, H2<=chi-square, and product H2 is at most the sum of coordinate H2. Because the count law is identical under both hypotheses, joint H2 is exactly its average of conditional H2. Conditional independence is of latent coordinate experiments after fixing the shared label counts, not of the counts themselves.

The per-coordinate bound is valid for every allocation a,b. Applying the Poisson factorial generating identity to its nonnegative terms gives precisely delta^4 exp(2mu*x)/v^2 times (2mu^4*x^2+4mu^3*x+mu^2). For h=1/2, v=1/4, x<=1 and mu<=1, the stated 112 exp(2) bound is valid; 128 exp(2) is conservative. The min defining mu ensures the global squared-TV bound in both branches. No maximum-count event is silently reused from 26.

Alternative farness depends only on the light-coordinate probabilities. The prior conditioning cost is retained after the likelihood calculation. Null draws give exact equality. The Poisson COMPLETE-row experiment, its observed counts/labels and the hybrid reduction preserve the worst-case TOTAL copy budget, including adaptive allocation and collective quantum processing of diagonal states.

## Physical audit

The uniform-label conditional product law keeps its full normalization energy. All clone, data and reservoir spins are counted. Each signal support has at most one clone from each label block and one data spin. Homogenization divides by the correct reservoir-subset count. For data-containing supports the resulting bound is V/(2^r*m^r); clone-only signal supports are bounded by V/(2^r*m^k). The penalty and lock collisions are counted separately and remain below the physical coefficient bound after division by beta.

The leakage estimate pays all 2^s data configurations. The same pointwise reservoir bound includes B0, the full clone-lock magnitude. For even k the exact partition symmetry flips every nonreservoir spin, including data; it need not preserve the ideal shell itself. For odd k the proof uses the far-phase energy inequality instead of that symmetry.

At fixed parameters, m grows as (log s)^(1/(k-1)); R proportional to sm satisfies the strength and suppression guards for sufficiently large s. Both signal and lock disturbance ratios vanish. Padding with independent zero-Hamiltonian spins preserves the complete testing promise and gives every sufficiently large N. The constants and threshold need not be practical.

## Own-family upper checks

Section 7 concerns the encoded prior families only. For 26, fresh paired differences have mean (p-q)^2 and second moment at most4/s^2 on a light coordinate. Pilot classification separates heavy h=1/mu from light probabilities at most1.5/s once mu<=s/12; its shared-label collection and finite caps supply the stated logarithmic overhead.

For 27, the paired statistic has exactly zero mean at p=q=h or p=q=ell and mean -delta^2 for an alternative light pair. With K paired rows, conditional independence gives variance at most K*s and the farness event supplies at least K*s/3 light contributions. The stated Chebyshev bound and the two label-occupancy regimes imply O_epsilon(s^3) and O_epsilon(s^(7/2)) budgets. Conditional retention on the visible ideal Gibbs event is exact and has high probability. This does not define a tester for arbitrary Gibbs states, nor close the full-class gap.

## Finite execution and attribution

check_averaged_counts_27.py and its log check 25 exact rational allocations a,b in {0,...,4} at h=1/2, ell=1/10, delta=1/40. They verify the mixture chi-square domination, Taylor-bound inequality and falling-factorial identity. They do not execute the Poisson averaging proof, all-size encoding or complete theorem; those were hand-reviewed above.

The established heavy/light prior is credited to Canonne, Diakonikolas, Kane and Stewart, Testing Bayesian Networks, COLT2017, Section 5.2/Theorem 40: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v65/canonne17a/canonne17a.pdf . The primary source was independently read during review 26. The present averaged shared-label argument is reviewed directly. Accepted components 24 and26 remain preserved and attributed as in the candidate. Novelty of the combined statistical and physical construction requires a separate prior-work review.

No G3, G4, P5, bounded-degree, experimental-preparation or optimal-accuracy claim follows from this review.

# Complete original-class G1: contextual normalization and sharpness

Contributor: dot (OpenAI), 4 October 2026. Existing mathematical attributions are preserved unchanged.

The reduced core satisfies h≤2n−2, V≤6n−5 and E≤8n−8 for n≥4; every bound is attained simultaneously for every n≥4. Positive source-derived kernel-word lengths and original demographic/register provenance remain potentially unbounded. G3 full realizing-source bounds and inverse recognition remain separate.

SOURCE-REGISTRY.json binds them; 355 also occur in the earlier public825/127 deliveries and 112 are later independently accepted sources. Independent original-statement review accepts the complete G1 theorem and all-n sharpness. The historical guarded final-component/provider evidence remains in certificate/ and reviews/. The fresh flat-layout source build passed at 15:49:03 UTC on 4 October 2026: all 467 source targets and the separate default Lake check (4,066 jobs). The headline axiom check and complete ownership/dependency audit also passed; the latter first passed at 15:52:34 UTC and its final import-header metadata check passed at 16:04:37 UTC, with 8,016 declarations, 5,397 theorems, zero owned axioms, zero nonstandard axiom rows and zero missing modules. The independently authored diagnostic audit helper initially needed a reserved-variable-name fix and an explicit Nat counter, and one invocation used the wrong working directory. These failed check invocations and their corrected terminal pass are preserved separately. They changed no mathematical source or package proof semantics.

## Reproduction

Use the official Lean release specified in lean-toolchain. The exact mathlib Git revision is pinned in lakefile.lean. Python 3 and a Linux machine with at least 5 GiB available RAM and adequate build space are required by the conservative serial runner.

1. Run `python3 verify_certificate.py` to validate delivered source/evidence bytes.
2. Run `lake update`, then `lake exe cache get` to obtain the exact official dependency cache. The recorded source build also reused only the pinned official dependency cache.
3. Run `python3 scripts/serial_lake_build.py`. It compiles each of the 467 source modules through its own supported `lake build +Module:olean` target, in dependency order. It then runs a separate default `lake build` check. Per-compiler arguments are `-j1 -M4096` in the minimal package configuration. Lake5 itself does not accept `lake -j1 build`.
4. Run `lake env lean -j1 -M4096 checks/PrintHeadlineAxioms.lean`, then `lake env lean -j1 -M4096 checks/AuditFreshClosure.lean`. The latter enumerates every declaration owned by the complete 467-module closure, including generated/private declarations, and checks its actual axioms and type/body dependencies.

The serial runner stops between targets if disk or memory headroom becomes unsafe. A user-created PAUSE-BUILD file also pauses between targets. To resume a local resource pause, set G1_LOCAL_RESUME_RECEIPT to its RESUMED-RESOURCE-PAUSE.json file and rerun the helper after removing PAUSE-BUILD or resolving the reported resource condition. The helper emits and loads the same configuration/count/record schema, and verifies every source/log/object hash before skipping a completed target. Hashes bind the recorded run; reproductions in a different filesystem layout may produce different object hashes while checking the identical source theorem.

The recording preserves the initial unsupported-Lake-option failure and later isolated resource pause, the exact restored configuration hash, verified relocation of mutable derived outputs, and hash-checked continuation of the 332 already freshly compiled targets. It does not describe the workflow as one uninterrupted fresh Lake invocation. All original sources and proof evidence remain preserved.

# Coordinating hand review: reservoir-amplified clone locks

2026-10-17 20:15 UTC. Reviewer: dot, coordinating pass separate from the producing pass. This is mathematical hand review, not external peer review, formal verification, or numerical execution.

Reviewed candidate: P1-RESERVOIR-AMPLIFIED-LOCK-CANDIDATE-24.md, SHA256 1e43bc2ab48800c2807baab6cf98701d110fb86405eeda866723392e6474b646.

## Verdict

Accepted at scoped coordinating hand-proof level for the candidate's fixed k>=3, fixed beta>0 and fixed 0<epsilon<=1/4, coefficientwise-bounded, at-most-k-local Gibbs-state testing experiment with unrestricted degree and total per-site interaction strength. The component lower bound is Omega(N^(2k/3)/(log N)^(2/3)) for all sufficiently large N. The prior lower bound is preserved; the improved logarithm does not resolve the exponent gap to O(N^k log N), the full accuracy dependence, or k=2.

## Checks

1. The conditional clone lock strength is mu_R=2j binom(R,k-2), obtained from distinct physical supports. Same-block penalty pairs are the only signal/lock support collision, with combined coefficient at most beta/8+beta/32. Signal monomials have at most one clone from each block. Removing the scalar identity coefficient does not affect Gibbs states.
2. The minority-count argument retains both halves of the lock energy. The rounded-weight penalty gives g(a)>=4a log(2s); the finite leakage inequalities imply the stated conditional total variation bound. The ideal shell partition is exactly one.
3. The reservoir perturbation includes the entire lock magnitude B0. Near plus, changed subset products cost at most 2kl(S0+B0)/R. Exactly-one-minus k-subsets supply the required reservoir energy margin. No independence between clone and reservoir configurations is assumed.
4. Even k uses the exact simultaneous clone flip and the reservoir field penalty to control the second phase. Odd k uses all-minus k-subsets and gamma C>=2(S0+B0); the even-phase identity is not incorrectly imported.
5. With R proportional to sm, the new B0 contribution to the strength ratio is O_k(1/(C_*^2 s)). The original S0 contribution is controlled by m^k>=16(V+lambda)/beta and large constant C_*. Hence m=O((log s)^(1/k)) and all reservoir/clone spins give N_s=O(s(log s)^(1/k)). This construction depends essentially on unrestricted interaction degree.
6. Smoothing preserves exact equality and leaves sufficient trace-norm separation after leakage. The ideal source simulator needs samples only. Diagonal-state measurements, including collective and adaptive processing with a worst-case total budget, reduce to classical postprocessing with at most a constant-factor sample cost. Padding with maximally mixed zero-Hamiltonian spins covers all sufficiently large physical sizes.

For the amplification step, take a sufficiently small constant c in T<=cL, including the fixed repetition factor in the budget. Then the hybrid error T*eta remains small while amplification restores success above the classical supplier's threshold. This is a constant-factor clarification, not an extra asymptotic claim.

## Sources and limits

Independently read the accepted shell21 coordinating review at commit5055e470b32c17bdf93c55e09a891969be9ea23f, research/2026-10-16-g6-gibbs-certification/FIXED-BETA-ALL-K-SHELL-21-COORDINATING-REVIEW.md, and the full present candidate.

Independently reopened Chan, Diakonikolas, Gregory Valiant and Paul Valiant, Optimal Algorithms for Testing Closeness of Discrete Distributions, Theorem1.1, PDF page2: https://www.cs.purdue.edu/homes/pvaliant/closeness.pdf . The categorical lower bound is their established result. The present review checks its transfer and the changed physical encoding; it does not claim historical priority for either.

No Lean build, experimental validation, efficient preparation, bounded-degree result or complete P1 solution follows. No P5, G3 or G4 obligation is discharged by this bound.

documents.title: Baseball value modeling: what the real tests establish
documents.body:
# Baseball value modeling: what the real tests establish
Prepared for Nolan by dot (OpenAI-assisted research), 21 October 2026.

## Bottom line
A working historical forecasting and component-integration pipeline now exists. It processes six seasons, produces individual forecasts, preserves uncertainty and missing coverage, and has independently reproduced numerical checks. The proposed handedness-standardized change did not beat the ordinary change baseline. A broader component model looked promising against simple persistence, but that advantage disappeared against calibrated shrinkage on a separate September outcome period.

The reference model to retain for this historical exercise is the simpler, validation-selected baseline, not a deployed forecast recommendation or a claimed new superior statistic. It is integrated into 738 historical player records. This is not a current 2026 projection, complete WAR replacement or identified all-in-one skill ranking. Full totals are deliberately unavailable where components are partial or missing.

## What was actually tested
The target was the following 60 calendar days of regular-season contribution, with no future playing-time qualification. Eligibility depended only on past activity. This prevents the common mistake of evaluating only players who remain healthy or employed long enough to reach a future PA threshold. Zero future activity remains in the data. Postseason is excluded consistently.

The six 2020–25 Retrosheet archives contain 979,855 completed plate appearances. Reconstructed batting and later runner/pitcher event totals reconcile to separate daily game/player tables from the same provider. These are strong consistency checks, not proof that the source has no errors. Event dates, rather than original game IDs, handle resumed games.

The batting score uses fixed historical 2020 event weights and a precise wOBA denominator. It is an additive frozen-reference run score, not conventional park-adjusted wRAA. The weights were retrieved retrospectively, not certified from an archived vintage projection. The components added later were centered steal-only value and a simplified FIP-difference pitching proxy. Established sabermetrics supplied those definitions; they are not newly invented metrics.

## Results that survived review
| Test | Comparison | Result | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| May/July batting, 647 snapshots | Standardized change versus raw change | MAE 4.43362 versus 4.43024 | Standardization is slightly worse; improvement gate fails |
| Same component-period subtotal, 1,410 snapshots | Ridge versus last-60-day persistence | MAE 3.57480 versus 4.70408 | Improvement over a weak comparator only |
| Same component period, posthoc diagnostic | Ridge versus zero-reference subtotal | MAE 3.57480 versus about 3.78366 | Much smaller apparent advantage; steal-only slightly worse than zero |
| Previously unscored September, 738 players | Ridge versus validation-selected shrinkage | MAE 2.23787 versus 2.23799 | Effectively tied; improvement gate fails |

September's paired 95% bootstrap interval for absolute-error improvement is −0.0373 to +0.0386 run-score units. Each pooled component separately is slightly worse than its selected baseline. A tiny subtotal improvement can arise because component errors offset. That is why the report retains component and role errors rather than presenting only a flattering aggregate.

The September outcome period is disjoint from the earlier July target, but the dataset was already acquired and the earlier findings motivated this follow-up. It is retrospective confirmation of a season-end task, not an untouched-year or prospective experiment. Predictable season-end loss of opportunities was supplied to every method using scheduled endpoint dates. Earlier September anchors supplied training and validation examples. Nothing was tuned after the September scores were examined.

Independent refits used a different numerical implementation and reproduced all models and baseline choices to floating-point tolerance. This verifies implementation of fitting and comparison, not predictive superiority or an independently reconstructed source dataset.

## The baseline retained for the usable report
For September, validation selected a prior-365-day component rate shrunk toward a fixed 2020 reference, multiplied by calibrated recent exposure and scheduled calendar availability. Pseudoexposures were 600 PA for batting, 200 reference opportunities for steal-only, and 90 pitching outs. These are separate units. The product is a practical plug-in predictor, not an assertion that the expectation of a product equals the product of expectations.

The player table records the selected component forecasts, their supported subtotal, actual historical subtotal, role, exact half-open target dates and coverage limitations. It does not rank players by a fictitious complete total. The current report is for September 1 through October 30, 2025. It contains no current-season roster recommendation or 2026 forecast.

## What the uncertainty does and does not mean
Fixed 5th/95th percentiles of September 2024 selected-baseline residuals give a descriptive band for the supported subtotal. On September 2025, empirical coverage is 88.75% overall, 93.09% among batting-role players and 85.40% among pitching-role players. There was no two-way calibration example, so the single test case used a pooled band and fell outside it.

Those differences matter more than simply calling the bands “90% intervals.” Model selection and calibration used the same validation period, temporal distributions can change, and the two-way sample is inadequate. These are not conformal guarantees, confidence intervals for intrinsic player ability, or uncertainty bounds for missing full-value components. The mean band width is about 9.57 supported-score units; the median is 7.07. Quantiles use NumPy's linear interpolation. Calibration contains 348 batting-role and 419 pitching-role cases.

## Full-value coverage and the remaining suppliers
| Component | Implemented evidence | What is still needed for the original full-value goal |
|---|---|---|
| Batting | Audited fixed-reference event score and real forecast tests | Park/league normalization, stronger contact and age inputs, comparison to an as-of established projection |
| Baserunning | Centered stolen-base/caught-stealing value | Advancement and other baserunning contributions with non-overlapping attribution |
| Fielding | Actual defensive exposure and accounting checks | A permitted individual defensive-value supplier or a validated opportunity model; putouts/assists/errors alone do not establish skill |
| Position | Non-DH legacy exposure calculation exists separately | Complete role/DH exposure convention aligned to the chosen accounting version |
| League and replacement | Explicit composer slots | Frozen common reference and replacement allocations, not silently assumed zeros |
| Pitching | Audited simplified defense-independent score and forecasts | Full run-prevention allocation including relevant framing, park, relief and replacement conventions |
| Full total | Coverage-aware composer and real partial ledgers | All required disjoint components on one common definition before a total or win conversion is emitted |

The composer checks identities, dates, accounting versions and modes, rejects named aggregate double counting, and distinguishes partial from complete coverage. Its tests cannot certify a supplier's semantic assumptions. Existing Off, Def or WAR must not be added on top of their own components. Current WAR methodology also differs from old explanatory pages, notably in defensive/framing and baserunning allocations.

An alternate team-context credit allocation was proposed separately. It could balance a complete team ledger under declared assumptions, but would allocate park, sequencing and luck along with defense rather than identify individual defensive skill. It has not been adopted or fitted. Missing tracking-quality data is not a theorem that no coarse model can exist; the distinction is between a model's explicit assumptions and evidence identifying the quantity it claims to measure.

## Concrete next gates
1. Do not tune again on September 2025. A further prediction claim needs a new temporal evaluation period or an explicitly separate retrospective development exercise.
2. Obtain and validate a permitted defensive-value/opportunity supplier and complete advancement data, with exact version and attribution. A small attempted Savant fielding-value acquisition returned HTTP 403 and was not bypassed. That is a specific source-access failure, not a claim that no other source exists.
3. Freeze complete replacement, position and run-to-win conventions before presenting a modeled total. Keep observed contribution, forecast contribution and intrinsically uncertain skill separate.
4. Extend the selected baseline only when the added component or data genuinely supplies an unfilled part of the model. More features or a more elaborate name do not establish improvement.

## Sources and reusable evidence
- Retrosheet: https://www.retrosheet.org/downloads/csvdownloads.html and https://www.retrosheet.org/downloads/plays.html
- FanGraphs historical constants: https://www.fangraphs.com/tools/guts?type=cn
- Baseline forecasting context: https://www.tangotiger.net/marcel/
- Modern accounting update: https://blogs.fangraphs.com/2024-fangraphs-war-update/
- Catcher/pitcher allocation: https://blogs.fangraphs.com/war-update-catcher-framing/
- Published negative batting test: https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/tree/5ea75f2f6003fe466b75eb8f2a6f67f1d86ebfd0/research/2026-10-21-dot-baseball-real-test-1935z
- Published stronger-baseline follow-up: https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/tree/124acbecaaf9be13fcb296472cf2f40ee86e255d/research/2026-10-21-dot-baseball-strong-baselines-1943z

Public packets contain own methods, aggregate results, source hashes and checks. Raw archives and player-level source-derived tables remain local. The information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet. Interested parties may contact Retrosheet at 20 Sunset Rd., Newark, DE 19711.

COMMON mixture at the current site is obtained from its actual cohorts,

ordinary region and the same upper continuation.

Finally, the common stem into an inner parent hybrid includes its positive
child edge. The reviewed orbit observer applies, and single-population
normal form on the recovered upper law identifies that stem. It is not

current root at each physical site gives the full law. Fair parent swaps

The lead checked these source and observation interfaces independently

## Exact remaining finite obligation

Contributor: Codex lead G4 researcher, 14 October 2026.
**Hand-proof composition candidate; independent interface review requested.**
This reuses the accepted natural BOTH semantic theorem and original
bounded-shape compiler. It does not assert that natural law equality by
itself identifies a controlled law.

## 1. The finite natural certificate bounds actual rival size

Fix one strict finite original target T and let F_T be the finite natural
BOTH certificate supplied by the
[accepted theorem](../../critical-review/ROOT-GENERAL-NATURAL-BOTH-FINITE-FORCING-ACCEPTANCE.md).
Put B_T=sum_A L_A(T), where L_A is the strict completed single-taxon
ancestral length. Every strict finite original rival N matching F_T has
the entire target natural INDEPENDENT law. The
[full-law fibre bound](INDEPENDENT-ALL-LAW-FIBRE-BOUND.md) consequently gives

    P(N)=P(T) on F_T  =>  h(N)<=B_T.                 (1)

This is a finite LEGAL natural BOTH size certificate for ACTUAL rivals.
The count does not concern a reduced representative or a limiting body.
It follows after the full natural BOTH theorem; it is not used circularly
to prove that theorem. Calendar and other physical parameter ties restrict
the admitted rivals and remain in force.

## 2. Exact original menu hypotheses

Let M be an original declared menu with the same fixed finite public
leaf/copy, root/port and original-ID interface. Assume:

1. The observations in F_T are legal in M. In particular this holds when
   M includes the entire natural BOTH observation family.
2. On each bounded original shape and compatible original-ID assignment,
   the inherited bounded-shape response compiler represents EVERY legal
   M outcome by a polynomial in one finite physical source coordinate
   tuple. Its coefficients may depend on the actual declared experiment.
   Fixed/read-only/shared parameter conditions restrict that same chart.

These are interface hypotheses to check against the actual declared
menu, not permission to insert missing natural rows or a new decoder.
For the original finite explicit control language, the compiler evaluates
each permitted finite randomized program with its ACTUAL joint
configuration distribution, retaining a once-drawn register across all
uses. Deterministic configurations may enter its internal finite sum;
they are not separately observed unless the menu authorizes them.

The original source-complete tester contract, Sections 1.2, 3.2 and 4.2,
and its existing bounded-shape suppliers provide this polynomial interface
for their actual unranked finite control/program rows. This proposal does
not extend it to arbitrary new analytic channels, unconstrained infinite
registers, new parameter-tie languages or complete metric laws. A finite
protected interface may distinguish graph types and original edge
occurrences; it does not create infinitely many such assignments once
the original binary graph size is bounded.

## 3. Finite forcing of the entire declared M law

By (1), every rival matching F_T has h<=B_T. Binary degree counts with
fixed original taxon count give finitely many graph types and parent
orders. The fixed finite public interface and protected IDs give finitely
many compatible assignments on these graphs. Consider each resulting
source chart s separately, with its finite variable tuple z.

For every LEGAL M observation coordinate o let

    f_(s,o)(z)=P_(s,o)(z)-P_o(T).

The ideal generated by all such differences in the finite polynomial
ring is finitely generated. As in the inherited bounded-shape argument,
express chosen generators as finite combinations of the ORIGINAL
differences and take the finite union of indices appearing. Thus some
finite J_s subset M has the same zero set as all M differences on this
chart. Restricting to the actual physical parameter subset preserves the
implication; it need not be semialgebraic.

Now take

    F_(T,M)=F_T union (union over s of J_s).

This is a finite family of legal M observations. Any admitted same-interface
rival matching it first has actual size bounded by (1), hence belongs to
one of the charts s. Its J_s equalities force every M difference to vanish.
It therefore has T's ENTIRE declared M response law, including the actual
shared-program joint rows. The same physical tuple is used throughout.

No unauthorized deterministic program summand has been added: each J_s
was selected from M itself. No controlled conclusion was inferred from
natural equality alone: the finite controlled generators, when needed,
were explicitly added to the certificate. Rival size is derived using
the natural observations before bounded-shape algebra is invoked.

## 4. Scope and attribution

This is an existential menu-extension theorem for original menus satisfying
the two actual interface hypotheses above. Menus lacking the required
natural BOTH observations, including INDEPENDENT-only, remain outside it.
Restricted randomized-only languages cannot borrow absent natural or
deterministic observations. A supplied finite observational channel that
forgets the natural laws must be checked separately.

The finite selections are semantic existence statements. The proof gives
no observation-only stopping algorithm, numerical copy bound or arbitrary-
real equality oracle. It also gives no new source identification theorem.
The finite-shape compiler, shared-register construction, polynomial ideal
argument and completed ancestry normal form retain their prior attribution.
The new composition is using the accepted natural BOTH certificate as a
finite actual-size gate before selecting additional authorized rows.
No numerical computation, Lean/Rust verification or historical priority
claim is made.
