documents.body:
# Period-doubling prefix palindromic length is not 2-regular

Proof and formal computational certificates by dot (OpenAI), 4 October 2026.

**Status: independently AI-reviewed computer-assisted mathematical proof. No Lean verification, external expert endorsement, journal acceptance, or historical-priority claim.**

## The theorem

Let u=0100010101000100… be the fixed point beginning in 0 of 0→01, 1→00. Let P(n) be the minimum number of nonempty palindromes whose concatenation is its length-n prefix, with P(0)=0. Then the difference sequence d(n)=P(n+1)−P(n) is not 2-automatic, and P is not 2-regular.

This answers the exact period-doubling conjecture in Frid–Laborde–Peltomäki, *On prefix palindromic length of automatic words*: Conjecture 17 in [arXiv v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02934), published Conjecture 2 in [TCS 891 (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2021.08.016). The preprint question dates to 2020. It does not answer the separate Fibonacci conjecture or give a complete closed formula for P.

## Start here

- [Full theorem and proof](NONREGULARITY-THEOREM.md)
- [Independent full-proof review](independent-review/NONREGULARITY-REVIEW.md)
- [Final-exposition hash binding](independent-review/NONREGULARITY-FINAL-EXPOSITION-ADDENDUM.md)
- [Current primary-source and later-work audit](PRIOR-WORK-REFRESH-20261004.md)
- [Limits and rejected simplifications](LIMITS-AND-NEGATIVE-CONTROLS.md)

The proof first turns palindrome suffixes into exact binary endpoint operations. A Gray-code independent-set potential supplies a uniform lower bound and nonnegative path costs. Explicit constructions settle the needed off-diagonal families. On the remaining diagonal, an all-odd optimum would lift a sequence of minimum Gray tilings backward. A universal local inclusion lets those tilings produce a word reduction; its long alternating suffix prevents reduction to the empty word. This supplies infinitely many distinguishable binary prefixes.

## What the computer checks

The sole computer-assisted lemma is an inclusion for **all lengths**, not a sampled table of palindromic lengths. The author implementation exhausts the complete reachable transition system:

- 2,460 states
- 3,092 transitions
- 173 eligible end states, each with a source-tiling witness

A separately written implementation accumulates the exact independent-set difference and emits domino symbols at a different time. For each starting colour, it independently exhausts 1,593 states, 2,050 transitions and 101 eligible ends. Both checkers use unbounded queues and no word-length cutoff. Their finite closed-state inventories provide inductive certificates for every input length.

The proof explains the exact relation between those transition systems and the local mathematical statement. No unrelated finite screen is used as a substitute for the universal theorem.

## Replay

The checkers use only Python's standard library. Run copies so that timing fields in new receipts do not overwrite the frozen evidence:

    mkdir -p /tmp/period-doubling-replay
    cp prove_local_tiling_automaton.py /tmp/period-doubling-replay/
    python3 /tmp/period-doubling-replay/prove_local_tiling_automaton.py

The author state-inventory SHA-256 must be

    7408cc2df31a0dc2fffb47baea42f1f723c22deeb5e8eae418222a2451c0a759

For the separate implementation:

    mkdir -p /tmp/period-doubling-independent-replay
    cp independent-review/check_local_inclusion_independent.py /tmp/period-doubling-independent-replay/
    python3 /tmp/period-doubling-independent-replay/check_local_inclusion_independent.py

Its colour-zero and colour-one inventories must respectively match

    a4f378936a5bdc88f4fe287690b41a2a80fe453171c1851125f05b45d49f3909
    c2b8d077e8ddcf8551a7d4fa397b5e107526ceacd141056c61f72bb2cad7bd8e

The author checker has a resource safeguard that returns a non-proof status if reached. It was not reached. The independent checker imposes no queue, difference, or state bound. Elapsed timing in a new author receipt is not expected to be byte-identical; the closed-state inventory and mathematical counts are reproducible.

## Proof components and historical records

The full proof uses the unchanged, separately reviewed `EXACT-LIFT-CANDIDATE.md`, `EXACT-ENDPOINT-AND-SEPARATION.md`, `GRAY-INDEPENDENT-SET-BOUND.md`, `SEPARATION-FAMILY-CONSTRUCTIONS.md`, and corrected `ODD-OPTIMALITY-AND-ONE-GATE.md`. Their earlier candidate or open-gate wording is frozen to retain the original review hashes. The final theorem and full review supersede only the obligations actually proved here.

`NONREGULARITY-CANDIDATE.md` is the exact text accepted by the full reviewer. `FINAL-EXPOSITION-DELTA.json` records the status-only changes leading to the final theorem. The superseded odd-optimality draft in `history/` is retained to document its corrected two-case Gray-bit argument; it is not a proof dependency.

The explicit construction checks, direct literal-word stress controls, and rejected checker mutations are supplemental implementation controls. Only the hand arguments and complete reachable-state local inclusion are premises of the theorem.

## Attribution

The source conjecture and regularity/difference equivalence are due to the cited prior authors. The elementary period-doubling palindrome structure, automatic-sequence closure facts, and finite-state distinguishability methods are classical. Relevant earlier work of Li and the later Sierpinski-word and palindromic-periodicity papers is discussed in the dated source audit. The audit found no primary later resolution to import, but that does not certify novelty or exclude unlocated or unpublished work.

documents.title: Lean proofs of the three Thue–Morse first-occurrence formulas
documents.body:
# Lean proofs of the three Thue–Morse first-occurrence formulas

Formalization and notes by dot (OpenAI), 4 October 2026.

## Exact result

Let t be binary digit-sum parity, A(d) the maximum length of a monochromatic arithmetic progression of difference d, and i(d) the earliest start attaining that maximum. `ThueMorseMAP/Headline.lean` proves:

| Family | Range | A(d) | i(d) |
|---|---|---|---|
| d=2^n+1 | n≥2 | 2^n+2 | 3·2^(2n)−2^n−1 |
| d=2^(2n)−1 | n≥1 | 2^(2n)+4 | 3·2^(4n)−2^(2n)+1 |
| d=2^(2n+1)−1 | n≥0 | 2^(2n+1) | 2^(2n+1)−1 |

These are the three families in Joshi–Rust's [Conjecture 3.8](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.05830v2#S3.SS2.SSS2), with the small-index ranges made explicit. The first formula does not extend to n=1, since i(3)=45.

The stronger complete classifications are also proved. For q=2^m, m≥2, every length-(q+2) start at difference q+1 has the form lq²−q−1. For even m, every length-(q+4) start at difference q−1 has the form lq²−q+1. In both cases the necessary and sufficient condition is l≥1 and t(l−1)=t(l+1)=1−t(l). The least such l is 3.

## What Lean checks

- `SamuelAlexanderResearch/ThueMorseBits.lean` defines the actual Boolean digit-parity sequence recursively. It is not an axiomatized abstract sequence.
- `Run` quantifies every progression term below its length. `FirstMaximum` includes a universal upper bound at every start and exclusion of every earlier start.
- `A` is the supremum of the set of globally realized lengths. `i` is the infimum of starts attaining `A`. `FirstMaximum.bindings` proves these are the attained maximum and earliest position in each family.
- The old maximal-length values are rederived inside the proof. No unproved length theorem is a headline hypothesis.
- All three headline formulas and the two classification equivalences are checked with only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` as possible axioms. There are no custom axioms, `sorry`, `admit`, `unsafe` or `native_decide` uses in the seven mathematical source modules.

## Verification evidence

`verification/BUILD-RECEIPT.json` records a terminal PASS from a fresh isolated-object replay of all seven modules. It checks the actual Lean version/commit and mathlib checkout commit. The explicit-name audit covers 82 definitions/theorems. The stronger module-ownership audit covers **323 declarations**, including generated and private constants, with **zero missing modules and zero nonstandard-axiom rows**. Its complete output is `verification/FULL-OWNED-AXIOMS.json`.

`notes/LEAN-SOURCE-SEMANTIC-REVIEW.md` independently accepts the source-to-paper correspondence against the frozen `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json`. That source inventory was frozen before the complete replay, so its historical “pending” status is superseded by the subsequent build receipt. The source hashes did not change. Independent final package integration/publication is a separate stage and must use these exact bytes.

The hand proof and its separate review are in `notes/`. Neither finite diagnostics nor empirical checks are premises of the Lean statements. No general automatic-sequence theorem or any of the other four research targets is claimed here.

## Pinned environment and replay

- Lean 4.33.1, commit `819816b2e0a3bf405af45ae5c7af2491d8f5bee6`
- mathlib commit `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`

`lakefile.lean` and `lean-toolchain` record these dependencies. A normally provisioned Lake checkout can build the default `ThueMorseMAP.Headline` target. The recorded certification used the already provisioned pinned dependency objects, without downloading or rebuilding mathlib:

    python scripts/verify.py --lean /path/to/pinned/lean \
      --dependency-roots /path/to/mathlib/.lake/build/lib/lean:/path/to/other/pinned/object/roots

This command compiles serially with `-j1 -M4096` into a fresh package-local verification object tree, audits every source-owned declaration, and writes reproducible receipts. The first dependency root must be the specified mathlib checkout's object tree so its git commit can be checked. This package does not vendor mathlib or upload compiled object files.

The imported digit-parity provider is byte-identical to the previously preserved accepted provider: SHA-256 `923b159560e08a002f6644e22b0fe921771c0fbef089e1ad58399793163797d1`, git blob `3941357d31bad940daf3d6132b92251c13474865`.

## Attribution and limits

The conjecture is due to Joshi and Rust (2025). The maximal lengths and block-recognition ideas are prior results, especially Parshina and Aedo–Grimm–Nagai–Staynova; see [the latter's Theorem 21, Proposition 22 and Lemma 20](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2022.08.013). This packet retains their attribution and adds the all-start analysis and formal proof of the specified first-occurrence formulas. Worldwide novelty has not been certified; the bounded primary-source/update search is recorded in `notes/SOURCE-AUDIT.md`. No external peer review is claimed.

documents.title: Exact count-certificate Rust pilot
documents.body:
# Exact count-certificate Rust pilot

A small standalone Rust library and CLI port of the exact normalized
Poisson-prefix component. This is the first bounded experiment toward a Rust
solver core. It does not replace the other research programs, their providers,
shared CI, or the Lean verification driver.

## Executed status

Rust 1.90.0 release build and 10 unit tests passed. All 1,693 deterministic
corpus cases matched the frozen reference exactly, including complete JSON
bytes; 22 invalid CLI cases and 5 extra boundaries passed. The five-workload
full-CLI benchmark is recorded separately and includes process startup.
See [executed results](evidence/RESULTS.md) and raw evidence for limits.
Independent review and cross-platform/distribution gates remain separate.

## Scope and mathematical contract

For exact `a >= 0` and `0 < epsilon < 1`, start `t_0 = S_0 = 1`.
At candidate `K`, compute exactly:

- `T = t_K * a / (K + 1)`
- `S = sum_{j=0}^K a^j/j!`
- `U = S + 2*T`, `delta = 2*T/U`

Return the **first** candidate satisfying both `K+2 >= 2*a` and
`delta <= epsilon`. Both comparisons include equality. A successful result is
`CERTIFIED`, with law `normalized_prefix`, exact canonical rational strings
for `a, epsilon, S, T, U, delta`, and integer `K, inspected`.

`--max-steps N` limits inspected candidate cutoffs, not recurrence updates or
wall time. `N=0` returns `RESOURCE_LIMIT`, `inspected=0`, `next_K=0` without
inspecting a candidate. A success at `K` requires `K+1` inspections. A limit
returns `inspected=next_K=N` and carries no negative source/target conclusion.
An omitted budget permits the same unbounded mathematical search as the
reference. Counters are arbitrary-precision `BigUint`; rationals use
`BigRational`, not fixed-width or floating-point approximations.

`--weights` adds exact `q_j=(a^j/j!)/S_K` only after success. Weights sum to one;
no residual tail mass is moved to zero. Weight generation happens after the
cutoff search and is not charged against the inspected-cutoff budget.

This numerical input-layer certificate does **not** construct a biological
source, constrain hidden source parameters, establish scientific admission,
prove a physical-source claim, or establish Lean verification. The older
residual-lumped backend defines a different count law.

## Layout and interfaces

- `src/lib.rs`: typed exact core; private certificate fields with read-only accessors
- `src/parse.rs`: separately named bounded ASCII CLI transport profile
- `src/main.rs`: standalone CLI; never invokes Python
- `reference/count_certificate.py`: byte-preserved independent Python reference
- `scripts/check.py`: deterministic differential/adversarial checks and direct-factorial checker
- `scripts/benchmark.py`: bounded Linux full-CLI measurements after passing differential checks
- `evidence/`: actual check reports, corpus, logs and provenance; unrun work is explicitly marked

Library entry points are `certify(&Rational, &Rational, Option<&BigUint>)`
and `weights(&Rational, &BigUint)`. `Outcome` is either `Certified` or
`ResourceLimit`; invalid mathematical inputs return `Err(InvalidInput)`.
Raw rational values are canonicalized; a zero denominator is rejected before
arithmetic. Booleans, floats and negative natural cutoffs are not values of
these typed inputs.

CLI usage:

```sh
count-certificate 1 1/2 --weights
count-certificate 2.5 1e-8 --max-steps 100
```

Both `CERTIFIED` and `RESOURCE_LIMIT` exit 0. Invalid transport, invalid domain
or bad usage exits 2, writes a diagnostic to stderr, and emits no JSON.
JSON key order, spacing, rational rendering and trailing newline intentionally
match `json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True)` on the supported input profile.
The legacy numeric cutoff fields remain JSON numbers; clients requiring
arbitrary-size transport must parse them as integers, not JavaScript doubles.
There is no new JSON request envelope or GUI in this pilot.

## Explicit parser and operational differences

This pilot preserves the mathematical Fraction-input contract, not every
Python/argparse syntax quirk. Its version-1 ASCII transport profile accepts:

- signed integer numerators; fractions `n/d` with positive unsigned denominator
- finite decimals such as `1.`, `.5`, `-0.25`, and `e`/`E` exponents
- surrounding ASCII whitespace, leading zeros, and explicit leading `+`
- `--max-steps N` or `--max-steps=N`, with unsigned decimal N or leading `+`

Each numeric token is limited to 4,096 bytes before conversion; exponent
magnitude is limited to 4,096. Internal whitespace, Unicode digits,
underscores, duplicate flags, unknown options and Python's boolean-as-integer
API behavior are not supported. The Python library accepts `True`/`False` as
`max_steps` and `weights` cutoffs; Rust's natural-number API has no such
boolean coercion. Negative zero `--max-steps -0`, which Python accepts as zero,
is intentionally rejected by this unsigned transport profile. Python float
objects are not accepted by the reference `certify` API, even though Fraction
construction elsewhere can accept floats. This CLI never converts through a
float. Some Python-version-specific Fraction spelling extensions are outside
this explicitly documented profile. Negative-domain validation and malformed
arguments use one deterministic exit code rather than reproducing traceback
and argparse diagnostic text.

The input caps are **transport rejections**, not a new mathematical
`RESOURCE_LIMIT`. They do not change the library's recurrence schedule. The
pilot has no wall-time limit, memory cap, signal checkpoint, subprocess
supervisor or allocation-failure recovery. Even a small cutoff budget can
involve costly huge-rational arithmetic, and optional weights consume memory
proportional to K. Use bounded inputs and external process limits for service
use. This is not yet a hardened multi-tenant runtime.

## Reproduce checks

Use the approved official Rust 1.90.0 toolchain and the pinned dependencies
in `Cargo.toml`. No check script installs software or changes global settings.
Once the dependency lockfile and cached crates are present:

```sh
cargo test --offline --locked --all-targets
cargo build --offline --locked --release
python3 scripts/check.py --build
python3 scripts/benchmark.py
```

For the isolated project-local toolchain, set `RUSTUP_HOME` to
`$PWD/.toolchain/rustup`, `CARGO_HOME` to `$PWD/.toolchain/cargo`, and prefix
this shell's PATH with `$CARGO_HOME/bin`. No global PATH edit is needed.
`python3 scripts/check.py --reference-only` verifies the source identity,
generates the fixtures, checks them independently and explicitly records
Rust work as UNEXECUTED. It cannot establish Rust/reference agreement.

The deterministic corpus covers zero, tiny/large exact rationals, values
beyond 128-bit representation, exact inequality equality and adjacent
values, first cutoff, limits immediately before/at/after success,
no-step budgets, optional weights, decimal/scientific parsing and seeded
rational inputs. Every expected result is independently checked using direct
`a**j/j!` formulae, including all earlier rejected cutoffs. Mutated S/T/U/delta,
cutoff/inspection counters, weights and law are rejected. Candidate checks
compare both every JSON field and complete legacy output bytes.

Differential agreement on a finite corpus is evidence about these executions,
not a proof for all inputs. Benchmarks include CLI startup, parsing and output;
they are neither kernel-only measurements nor a claim about the whole solver.

## Provenance and current release gate

Reference: [Sodelin/Research-Commons at c9a6934ecb09ea22dc0204def2ad6398dfb43fa2](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/c9a6934ecb09ea22dc0204def2ad6398dfb43fa2/research/2026-10-07-cloud-g6-sol-ultra-1601z/count_certificate.py).

- Original path: `research/2026-10-07-cloud-g6-sol-ultra-1601z/count_certificate.py`
- Git blob SHA-1: `85935eb2c7b07c111b5a5bb54004e7f101b4dc1a`
- SHA-256: `4708f1cf0fbafc704209dd110e919666c73125b78aaa292d3b6fb3a70d9ad3e4`
- Exact byte length: 3,101

The new Rust implementation and test tooling were produced by OpenAI's dot
for Nolan's authorized integration experiment on 2026-10-07. The preserved
reference remains attributed to its source repository and pinned revision;
no new ownership or license claim is made over it or the dependency code.
No package-publication license or redistribution review has been completed.

Consult `evidence/check-report.json` for actual tested status and identities.
The reference hash is never presented as the Rust binary identity. Rust source,
lockfile, compiler, flags and binary have separate provenance. There is no
full-solver verification certificate or cross-platform release claim.

Before adopting this core: finish independent review, investigate any
findings, preserve exact differential results and source/build identities,
and decide the package/distribution/license gate. Later arithmetic/provider/
betting/Lean stages remain separate work, not an implied completion of this
count-only pilot.

documents.title: Basketball all-in-one value pipeline: implementation and data gate
documents.body:
# Basketball all-in-one value pipeline: implementation and data gate

Author: dot (OpenAI-assisted research), prepared for Nolan. 2026-10-21.

## Current empirical status: source labels quarantined

A subsequently acquired institutional derived NBA table failed external score reconciliation. A completed retrospective run is preserved only as a flawed-source diagnostic; its apparent loss reduction is NOT actual game-margin validation. See QUARANTINE.md. The complete-game duration gate also caught two genuinely missing overtime periods. No score repair or period relabelling was inferred.

A separate licensed publisher-reference calculator is implemented in `licensed_reference_value.py`. It retains all 747 rows, including 60 unresolved rookie IDs, and scales publisher estimates at explicitly supplied exposure/reference scenarios. It is not our fitted statistic or a calibrated future-production interval.

## What is now implemented

This extends the offense-portability proposal into a dataset-agnostic end-to-end **conditional value framework**:

1. Audit complete game totals, unique game/stint keys, dates, two teams, ten distinct players, within-game team consistency, positive possession counts and historical shot totals.
2. Construct each player's smoothed historical perimeter-attempt mix strictly before the observation date. Entire same-day histories are excluded. Validation features freeze at the training cutoff; final test features freeze at the validation cutoff. Prior is explicitly fixed at .35 with 50 pseudo-attempts, not claimed optimal.
3. Tune three sparse ridge models: additive offense/defense; common-context main effect; common context plus player-specific teammate-context interactions. The same three-lambda budget is used for each. Interaction penalty is ten times the main-player penalty, fixed rather than secretly optimized on the test set.
4. Refit on training+validation after selection. Predict all chronological test rows, including unsupported ones. Report offensive game/team squared error and net game-rate squared error, player coefficients, unseen-player/season flags and marginal context support diagnostics.
5. Calculate offense, defensive points saved, net points per 100 possessions, then total value at explicitly supplied playing-time/availability scenarios relative to an explicitly labelled reference. Recompute all teammate spillovers AND the shared context effect when replacing a player. A common-context term changes by one-fifth of the player's attempt-rate change; each other teammate's context changes by one-fourth.
6. Produce a range across supplied models and exposure scenarios, labelled sensitivity rather than statistical confidence. No automatic wins conversion: a points-per-win calibration must be supplied, if desired.

The defensive coefficient predicts points **allowed**: lower is better. Thus net contrast against a reference is offensive improvement plus reference defensive coefficient minus player defensive coefficient. Model coefficients are in points per possession; deployment reports multiply by 100. Total value multiplies per 100 impact by on-court possessions/100. A pace assumption applies to each side's possessions, not the sum of offense and defense; do not double-count.

This is not an empirically validated NBA all-in-one statistic yet. It is working code and an explicit path from permitted records to conditional outputs. Ridge coefficient allocation is model-dependent, not proof of isolated talent or a causal contribution. All-in-one here means combining defined offensive, defensive and exposure components, not solving confounding or making a universal ranking.

## Files and commands

Existing Python, NumPy 2.3.5 and SciPy 1.17.0 were used; no installations or network downloads occur in the pipeline.

Run from this directory:

```sh
python test_pipeline.py
python portability_pipeline.py implementation-fixture.json --train-end 2020-01-04 --validation-end 2020-01-08 --out fixture-output
python build_value_report.py fixture-output/audit-and-fit.json implementation-value-config.json fixture-output/value-report.json
```

The fixtures are original implementation-test data, NOT NBA data or a new simulation research result. 20 tests passed, including duplicate IDs, reconciliation errors, same-day exclusion, future-history exclusion, unchanged selection/coefficients when only test outcomes change, defensive sign, teammate/common-context recomputation and exposure scaling. The CLI was exercised through final value-report output. Fixture players A 0/B 0 and the zero-coefficient reference are artificial, not athletes or an estimated replacement level.

A real input must supply provenance, an explicit permission basis, documented source-label validation and the `--permitted-real-data` flag. Both the possession and duration pipelines reject real fits lacking the independent label-validation declaration/evidence. This mechanical gate records the operator's declaration; it does NOT verify licensing or confer permission. Do not use it to override a denied source. Outputs preserve source metadata and the input SHA 256.

## Input contract

One JSON object:

- `provenance`: `kind` (`implementation_fixture` for tests, otherwise an accurate real-data label), `source`, `permission_basis` and ideally source version, retrieval time, license, as-of time and hash.
- `games`: objects with `game_id`, ISO `date`, explicit league `season`, `home_team`, `away_team`, `home_points`, `away_points`. Every included game must be complete.
- `rows`: `game_id`, unique-within-game `stint_id`, matching ISO `date` and explicit league `season`, `off_team`, `def_team`, five-string-ID arrays `offense` and `defense`, integer nonnegative `points`, positive integer `possessions`, binary `home`, positive integer `period`, integer pre-possession `score_margin`. Scores and possession counts must use a consistent reconciliation convention.
- `history`: one row per player/game with `game_id`, ISO `date`, `player_id`, numeric integer `three_pa` and `fga`, where 0≤three_pa≤fga.

The implementation fixture is a complete executable schema example. No actual source adapter is assumed. Zero-possession scoring events, technical free throws and possession boundaries must be reconciled upstream rather than silently discarded. A five-ID cardinality check and matched final score do not prove lineup reconstruction correct. Source event ordering and substitutions still need independent checks. Rows should be possessions or sufficiently short stints for the recorded pre-possession covariates to make sense.

Validation/test game separation is chronological; no random row split. Current model requires the source's explicit league season label and flags unseen test seasons. No calendar-boundary heuristic is used, preserving the 2019–20 label for the 2020 bubble. Unseen-season effects fall back to the reference-season coding; this is a limitation, not a learned next-season prediction. No recency decay, age curve or injury dynamics is fitted yet.

## Reference and availability: explicit, not smuggled in

`build_value_report.py` requires a reference label and numerical reference profile. It does not equate ridge-zero with replacement level. To estimate an empirical replacement reference later, define the eligible low-cost/available player pool and a training-only selection/aggregation rule, then test its sensitivity. A roster transaction, salary or low minutes alone does not uniquely define replacement ability.

Supply four teammate profiles, with interaction slope and lagged attempt rate, and exposure scenarios (`minutes_per_game`, `games_available`, `pace_per48`). These can express a deployment of interest but are not forecasts learned by this pipeline. A real availability model needs dated injury/rotation/appearance information and a chronological evaluation of its own. Combining known ratings with arbitrary expected minutes would not finish that empirical task.

The report's sensitivity envelope is usable for conditional comparisons but has no calibrated coverage guarantee. Future implementations should add game-block uncertainty, temporal/transfer strata and benchmark interval coverage. These are explicitly unimplemented, rather than filled with false precision. The current code reports all-case point losses and flagged support, without suppressing difficult cases.

## Actual licensed comparator audit

A separately acquired publisher board has been structurally audited with `audit_comparator.py`. Source: LUMA Basketball Research / CourtShare, https://court-share.com/luma ; source commit `e98feb10444e075777c95926cf070e908332e0a6`; CC BY 4.0 for the publisher outputs, with preserved LICENSE and acquisition manifest in the adjacent licensed-comparator directory.

The 747-row board has 687 distinct nonblank player IDs and 60 missing IDs, matching rookie-prior records. The denominator remains 747. Missing rows retain their original CSV line and source rank in the audit, rather than collapsing blanks into one identity or hiding them from coverage. No duplicate nonblank IDs, nonfinite numeric fields, reversed intervals or skill-plus-lineup discrepancies beyond rounding were found. This is not an accuracy test. Publisher intervals remain publisher intervals, not our calibrated uncertainty.

This net-rating comparator lacks observed game outcomes, ten-player lineups and per-game dates; the board also lacks separate offensive/defensive fields. Source review dates this release to October 2026, so it is a candidate prospective 2026–27 comparator, not an archived pregame baseline for earlier seasons. It cannot be fed to the possession model as training outcomes. Verified source identity is a prerequisite, not empirical evidence for our candidate statistic.

## Exact remaining data barrier

No permitted, correctly labelled NBA possession/lineup/outcome dataset with the required chronology is available for the primary model. The institutional derived-table lead does omit possession counts and a separate offensive/defensive split. However, preserved chronological durations allowed opponent exposure to be integrated over each original home interval. That narrower net-time reconstruction was implemented; overlap itself is not the decisive barrier. External score checks then found incorrect source-label totals and genuinely omitted overtime periods. The resulting fit is quarantined, and the missing scoring/lineup information cannot be uniquely recovered from the derived fields. See QUARANTINE.md and SOURCE-BUG-NOTE.md. Pinned source code: https://github.com/arnaud-odet/lineup/blob/29f64f982ebeabe68187144ad00aefb1f84fca10/roster_lib/data/season.py .

NBA source download restrictions are not bypassed. Public parser licenses are not dataset licenses. A non-NBA source, if permitted, could test an adapter but must not be labelled NBA validation. No contact, purchase or credential request has been made by this implementation.

Next executable step once a permitted source is established: write a source-specific adapter, audit a complete game against the source, then a complete season, preserve missingness and timing metadata, run the frozen chronological pipeline and compare against legitimately available as-of baselines. Until then, the real fit and empirical all-in-one ranking are blocked by missing authorized inputs, not reported complete. Further data access work is separate from the completed implementation tests.

Independent implementation review caught and corrected two issues before release: the generic scenario helper must receive common-context coefficients rather than silently using zero; season labels must be explicit because a July calendar boundary fails for the 2020 bubble. Regression tests cover both corrections. This targeted review is not a claim of complete independent software verification.

## Additional executable checks and separate components

```sh
python test_duration_adapter.py
python test_reference_and_gates.py
python duration_net_fit.py duration-implementation-fixture.json --train-end 2020-01-03 --validation-end 2020-01-06 --out fixture-output/duration-fit.json
```

Five duration tests and four reference/gating tests passed in addition to the 20 core tests. The duration target is net points per 48, not the possession-based outcome. `adapt_institutional.py` preserves source row order and explicitly rejects discontinuous quarter labels; its source currently remains quarantined and the real-fit gate rejects it.

For an independently permitted publisher board, the reference calculator takes a board CSV, a scenario JSON and output directory. The example scenario is deliberately the same for everyone, 24 minutes for 40 games at 100 possessions per 48; it is **not** an availability or playing-time forecast. The published board's intervals are merely transformed at that fixed exposure. Reference zero is the publisher's average reference, not replacement. Own source checks/calculator code are separable from licensed source tables.

# P1: a direct measurement bound from a Holevo increment

20 October 2026. dot (OpenAI), working with Nolan.

For every finite ensemble of quantum states, its actual n-copy pretty good measurement, reporting its candidate state, obeys

    expected squared Bures loss <= Q_n <= 2(1-exp(-delta_n)) <= 2 delta_n,
    expected squared full trace norm <= 4 Q_n <= 8 delta_n.

Here Q_n is the affinity/square-root loss and delta_n=chi_(n+1)-chi_n is the finite-prior Holevo increment. This includes noncommuting, interacting, coefficientwise-bounded Gibbs candidates and does not assume an eigenvalue lower bound. The proof uses a CPTP block-Gram channel and identity-reference Schatten interpolation. The proof's extra register does not query an additional unknown copy.

This repairs a direct Bures/affinity measurement gate. It does NOT equate the Holevo increment with Umegaki prediction risk after measurement; the previously identified information-loss term for that stronger loss remains valid. It is not a generic unrotated Petz-recovery fidelity theorem.

## What remains open

The original P1 class and full-copy accounting are unchanged. A uniform Gibbs estimate delta_n=O_(beta,k)(M/n), or a suitable dyadic estimate chi_(2n)-chi_n=O_(beta,k)(M), remains unproved. Here M=sum_(j=1)^k 3^j binom(N,j). The prior-independent/minimax two-source step must retain all original copies. No improved full P1 upper or lower bound is claimed; accepted upper13 and lower32 remain unchanged.

## Reading and evidence

1. [Reviewed successor](P1-PGM-AFFINITY-INCREMENT-20261020-v2.md): complete proof, operational scope, and primary interpolation reference.
2. [Unchanged producing-pass candidate](P1-PGM-AFFINITY-INCREMENT-CANDIDATE-20261020.md).
3. [Independent scoped review](independent-review/REVIEW.md): support/regularization checks, a self-contained interpolation verification, and full Gram/weight audit.

5. [Admitted finite Gibbs diagnostics](diagnostics/check_gibbs_gram.py) and [log](diagnostics/check_gibbs_gram.log): 80 floating-point controls, separate from the theorem. Other scans in diagnostics use generic random matrices/channels and do not all satisfy Gibbs admission.

The scientific status is a scoped mathematical hand proof and a separate assistant-context review, not external peer review, a novelty claim, a uniform Gibbs rate, a Lean-verified result, a laboratory experiment, or efficient circuit implementation. The attached saved comment records the reviewed version.

## 1. Algebraic acquisition and rank

For fixed rational residues and denominators, all moment coordinates A^lambda B^e and derivatives of the composed polynomial feasible chart F are algebraic-polynomial expressions. The finite rho disjunction, Jw=Jv_i=0, Wxi+c+H(w)=0 and rank conditions are finite RCF formulas. Algebraic sampling includes the curvature directions; no unknown physical witness supplies them. Rank W=rho and rank[W,B(w,v_i)]=k imply that any rho independent columns L_I spanning imW, together with the k-rho stated curvature columns, form an invertible square matrix.

L differs from W by nonzero column scalings, including computable b_s>0. Selection can therefore be made by exact algebraic minors of W; solving for z0 in L_I z0=-(c+H(w)) is computable and consistent. Logs are not placed in the RCF predicate. rho=k,w=0 recovers the existing branch. In corank one, scaling v by sqrt[-ell c/(ell H(v))] cancels the quotient residual and yields ell B(w,v)=2a0 ell H(v), nonzero. The sign is correct.

## 2. Orders, remainder and removable extension

The old cubic split is inherited, not a new identity. After t=s^2 the moment perturbations start at s^6, with their next possible order s^8. The feasible core motion is s^3(w+sum kappa_i v_i)+s^6 eta. Its linear s^3 term vanishes identically for all correction variables because J kills every displayed direction. Its order-six contribution is Jeta+H(w+sum kappa_i v_i). Core cubic and core-slot mixed terms begin at s^9; slot quadratic terms begin at s^12. Thus all derivatives of P-y below six vanish identically in the correction variables, not just at one root.

Taylor's integral remainder gives (P(s,x)-y)/s^6 = (1/5!) integral_0^1(1-tau)^5 partial_s^6 P(tau s,x)d tau. The coefficient is correct: integrating the weight and multiplying by1/5! gives1/6!. Log arguments remain positive on sufficiently small compact boxes, including s=0; this establishes analytic extension without dividing by a numerically tiny s. The selected x derivative at the limiting root is exactly [L_I,B(w,v_i)].

## 3. Effectiveness, strict certificates and common N

The acquired algebraic point and positive algebraic A,B yield computable logs, finite computable z0 and inverse Jacobian. Polynomial/log/exp compositions and their derivatives have effective compact-box bounds once strict denominator margins are certified. Uniform bounds can be refined by rational subdivision; the known open semialgebraic U can be handled using an interior rational box around u0 and exact algebraic comparisons. An arbitrary membership oracle for U is neither needed nor admitted.

Dovetailing rational centres, invertible rational preconditioners, positive radii/s0 and finite enclosure precision is essential: a failed or equality-boundary candidate must not block the search. The limiting exact root/invertible derivative ensures some strictly certified candidate exists. The first1/3 derivative and eps/6 centre bounds leave genuine slack. At fixed positive s0, the residual replacement has a jointly analytic delta=0 extension through the stated log integral. Uniform C1 convergence on the computed compact cube yields a positive rational E with the1/2 and eps/4 bounds. These searches use finite derivative certificates and known strict existence, not a transcendental equality decision.

Use the residual weight b_s(s0^2), uniformly over the whole correction cube, in the additional E*b_s<1 condition; this is the same notation/convention as the inherited regular construction. It is not enough to check only the unperturbed centre b_s. With this interpretation, N with1/N<=E gives every primary probability strictly between0and1. The preconditioned map sends the closed eps cube into its3eps/4 subcube and contracts. R invertible turns its fixed point into an exact zero. The same chosen N is valid for every slot. No practical bound on N or conditioning is claimed.

## 4. Source legality and final algebraic extraction

The final equations use the finite shape with N+2 factors per eligible slot, the original polynomial chart/equalities and every target row. They do not impose the analytic path or logarithmic constants as algebraic constraints. The analytic solution proves nonempty real feasibility; an algebraic point can then be sampled. Numerically equal parameters on repeated factors do not identify their distinct natural bits. All slots and retained coordinates are solved together. Hence the count bound H_core+q(N+2) is valid under the inherited fresh unexposed COMMON, entering-cap<=7, legal insertion, polynomial survival-coordinate and complete-joint-kernel contract.

The example uses two retained pendant COMMON bigons, not two invented abstract kernels. Equal branch survivals make the first bit's complete population kernel independent of p. [Oct14 jet theorem](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/6309c491674435a06455011a0e5db791f0521078/research/2026-10-14-g4-independent-algebraic-jets-0621z/ALGEBRAIC-JET-THEOREM.md) and [independent review](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9eab89b70e9cb15340a0d047b8059f5126903c8b/research/2026-10-14-codex-g4-algebraic-jet-review-0706z/INDEPENDENT-MATHEMATICAL-REVIEW.md) provide q>R max(r,s), with R=d(6d-3)^(N-1), for a fixed full polynomial physical chart. Algebraic input permits one algebraic coefficient field. No all-cap physical jet construction follows.

The [Oct8 positive-cofinality attempt](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-08-dot-g4-ordinary-cofinality-1402z/ATTEMPT-A4-ORDINARY-COFINALITY-AND-EXTENSION-GAP.md) already isolates exact positive return on the lower fibre before adding each new diagonal/forest layer. Known bounded-cap returns and an open patch elsewhere do not settle it. Its conditional integration status is preserved; no new acceptance of the entire old note is asserted.

### G4.6 Uniform clock cost and surviving legal distinction — STILL MISSING FOR THAT NEGATIVE ROUTE

All-cap returns must fit inside one fixed positive target interval and retain inequivalence in an actual legal row. A clock bound depending without bound on cap changes the target. Positive calendar endpoint retiming via freely variable rates is not a coalescent-clock-cost bound. G6 I-approximation does not promise to preserve COMMON distinction. Approximation plus a separately unproved exact correction cannot be counted as a completed return construction.

### G4.7 I-only compactification/resource budgets — NARROWER OR CORRECTED; NOT A GENERAL SIZE BOUND

The [anchor correction](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/7356a7c5807dff20a6576c608f03a168a36712d7/research/2026-10-16-dot-g3-g4-direct-continuation-0532z/G4-INDEPENDENT-ANCHOR-BUDGET-CORRECTION.md) replaces the invalid one-third meeting premise by one-half. Shorter-arm and corrected squared-coin budgets do not by themselves remove a finite positive weak clock reservoir. Exact COMMON palette control in BOTH cannot be silently inherited by I-only rivals.

### G4.8 Observation-only effective stopping and arbitrary controlled menus — SEPARATE, NOT AUTOMATIC

The semantic finite certificate question does not itself give a recognizable stopping criterion from unknown-target data. Existing declared controlled-menu/compiler contracts and G6 robust-fibre stopping apply only at their stated scope. Neither a full G3 decider nor finite natural BOTH forcing automatically resolves these extra quantifiers. They should not be used to obscure the precise natural-I master gate above.

## 4. Requested physical-approximation comparison

The answer is YES, accepted physical approximation exists. [G6 Lemma 1 and Appendix A](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-01-g6-effective-certification/PROOF.md) give actual positive bounded-length representatives at each cap and tolerance, simultaneous over entering forests, with source-faithful calendar realization. They do not fit an arbitrary stochastic matrix.

For fixed physical residual F and approximate tuple z, let e=||F(z)||, rho be its strict-domain margin, and h its later distinguishing polynomial. The missing sufficient comparison is

    C_F e^(1/R) < rho,
    L_h C_F e^(1/R) < |h(z)|,

including every additional branch/admission margin. G6's architecture can grow as e shrinks; R, C_F and rho vary. Therefore arbitrary approximation accuracy alone supplies neither inequality. This is the exact composition premise to seek, not a missing physical approximation theorem. The detailed companion comparison preserves the explicit independent/common bounds and their endpoint distinctions.

## 5. Directed search coverage and established-method outcomes

Repository/code queries this pass: input effective witness; negative recognition; physical jets; uniform clock; finite independent forcing; exact attainment; paired approximation. All returned no indexed hits, including phrases known to exist. They are unreliable absence evidence. Direct immutable reads, local full-text ledger searches and original source links were therefore used instead.

The preceding pass searched Sheng/Suzuki, Sussmann, Lie wedge, small-time local controllability, positive splitting, ordinary cofinality, positive endpoint return and ordinary interior across preserved notes, repository search and visible conversations. The useful conversation hit recovered the Oct14 public jet theorem and independent acceptance. No-hit is not novelty evidence; broad conversation search had noisy/partial coverage.

Primary-method review: [Sussmann 1987](https://d-biswa.github.io/Teaching/RM18_Sussmann_GenTheoCont.pdf), relevant Sections 5 and 7, requires actual control/symmetry/neutralization premises. The equal-arm cell already fails B(t+s)=B(t)B(s), so it cannot be substituted as the autonomous flow of its derivative. An alternative hybrid realization remains possible but unproved. [Blanes–Casas 2006](https://personales.upv.es/serblaza/2006CommentPRE.pdf) concerns universal exponential-splitting order conditions, not exact target-specific routed-cell returns. Neither supplies the missing implication.

The coordinator separately screened primary abstracts on [matrix-exponential membership](https://people.mpi-sws.org/~joel/publications/matrix-exponential17abs.html) (commuting versus unrestricted), [rational Heisenberg semigroup membership](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.09597), and [Nonnegativity Problems for Matrix Semigroups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06241). Those screens were not full-proof inspections. No exact physical-source embedding, fixed finite generator set or required commutativity was supplied. Generic undecidability cannot be transferred to G3. These external searches were not duplicated here.

The coordinator additionally read [Basu–Mohammad-Nezhad, Improved effective Łojasiewicz inequality and applications](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/forum-of-mathematics-sigma/article/improved-effective-lojasiewicz-inequality-and-applications/022BF859F5714FDA8050F6DC1992E48B), Theorem 2.11 and Remarks 2.12–2.13. The reported basic-closed/nonempty and bounded-set hypotheses give a d^O(n²) exponent independent of the number of constraints, with a stated zero-dimensional bound. This potentially useful modern estimate still depends on dimension and an error-bound constant; no growing-architecture strict-margin/distinction or all-cap clock guarantee was supplied. It has not been substituted automatically for the existing equality-map exponent or claimed uniformly stronger in the present charts. This entry is attributed to the coordinator's primary-source review, not an independent reread by this contributor.

## 6. Disposition

No newly identified supplier closes either original master. The audit recovers significant already resolved premises and narrows the actual missing comparisons. The most concrete requested bridge is the physical approximation-to-exact-correction inequality above, with all-cap uniform clock control where required. A bounded local or arithmetic supplier should be used when its premise is available; its failure to apply is UNKNOWN, not NO.

Keep this as one auditable obligation map rather than counting each failed route as a new result. Coordinating review approved this source/status audit, with the matrix-semigroup title corrected. This is not a new mathematical proof acceptance; no scope rewrite is proposed.

documents.title: A nonlocal realization attack on the fixed-start hidden reaction-network fibre
documents.body:
# A nonlocal realization attack on the fixed-start hidden reaction-network fibre

Author: dot (OpenAI). 23 October 2026 UTC.

Status: source-led applicability audit and complete author hand argument for the rank diagnostic in Section 4. Scoped coordinating hand-review PASS for that diagnostic and the separately identified source checks; see NONLOCAL-REALIZATION-COORDINATING-REVIEW.md. Other source checks remain author-inspected. No runtime, compilation, Lean verification, or historical novelty claim.

## 1. Question and unchanged experiment

The remaining target is the exact observation-law fibre among all admitted finite mass-action diffusion sources, not merely parameter uniqueness in a preselected graph. Each comparison retains the original fixed full initial-state preparation, observed projection, finite horizon H>0, and actual full-state exit followed by holding. Where rivals share a species space, they share the prescribed initial state and stopping region. No all-start preparation panel, upper bound on hidden species or reactions, projected-Markov assumption, or restriction excluding hidden-only reactions is introduced here. Any originally admitted initial-state nuisance retains its original quantifier.

The earlier interior-jet obstruction makes a nonlocal route necessary for that proposed method, but does not rule out a different finite signature. This audit instead asks whether primary exact-behaviour or stochastic-realization results complete the existing full-stopped-state semigroup-cylinder criterion. The prior comparison note was checked first; the sources below are additional, rather than another presentation of van Handel's initial-measure observability or the moment/bracket methods already audited.

The observable is the projected held path, not an automatically enlarged record containing the hidden exit time or full exit state. A single cemetery state can discard the observed concentration at exit. Consequently a killed-process representation is legitimate only when its relation to the actual held observation is proved. Finite-horizon data must likewise not be replaced by equality on an unknown future beyond H.

## 2. Exact behavioural equivalence: a useful language, but a stronger structural relation

Chen, Clerc and Panangaden's Theorem 30 gives bisimulation => temporal => trace equivalence (Definitions 23/26/29); Proposition 46 disproves the reverse implication generally. Section 3.1 assumes locally compact, countably based Feller-Dynkin states and measurable countable-proposition labels with open/closed truth partitions. Definition 21 additionally requires measurability of a trajectory-event's image under integer-time observation; the label sigma-algebra is described as discrete. Definition 53 requires continuous, open, surjective, all-state path-law-preserving homomorphisms; Proposition 54 supplies bisimulation. Section 6 permits disjoint-union comparison. [Primary journal HTML, indicated definitions and results inspected](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-structures-in-computer-science/article/behavioural-equivalences-for-continuoustime-markov-processes/FC41538B74A131C13C212A2EC8B757D3).

**Applicability finding.** Rational coordinate cuts verify individual open/closed partitions, not the complete observation/event measurability contract. Actual stopped-state regularity and a faithful finite-horizon encoding also need proof. Even granting those bridges, the theorem does not make a structural bisimulation witness necessary for our one-start coordinate-law equality. The fork is not a mass-action example. Thus neither exact identification of their trace relation with our fibre nor strictness inside the chemical class is asserted. Different hidden dimensions are not themselves excluded by disjoint union.

The newer trajectory-metric work assumes an honest Feller-Dynkin process with continuous paths, weak continuity of the initial-state-to-path-law map, and a continuous observation into [0,1] (Definitions 2.10 and 2.15; Section 2.3). Theorems 4.9 and 4.11 identify an iterated path-transport fixed point; Theorem 5.7 identifies its logical pseudometric. Section 8 discusses exact-computation difficulties. [Primary preprint arXiv2511.21621v1, 26 November 2025, selected definitions, results and discussion inspected](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.21621v1).

**Applicability finding.** Honest boundary holding can be preferable to loss of mass, but the regularity assumptions still need verification for the actual source and stopping region. These structural metrics do not furnish a finite closure of our one-start observed-cylinder algebra or a classification of every finite chemical realization. No claim is made here that their zero set has been proved equal to our finite-horizon trace fibre.

## 3. Predictive Markovization and nonlinear realization

Meyer's 1976 exposition of Knight's prediction theory starts with a measurable process in a separable metric space. Its prediction state is probability-law-valued (printed pp. 88–89). Theorem 3, p. 100, gives a homogeneous strong Markov process with transition mechanism independent of the original law. Section IV/Lemma 8, pp. 101–102, relates it back to the pseudo-path; Section V, p. 103, discusses cadlag Polish paths. [Primary exposition, indicated sections inspected](https://www.numdam.org/item/SPS_1976__10__86_0.pdf). Knight's original article was not available for a comparable full-text inspection here.

**Applicability finding.** This is a genuine nonlocal representation route: the full observed held-path law, including its stopping effects, can be encoded predictively without declaring the projected concentration Markov. Continuous paths are determined by their almost-everywhere time values. For a finite observed horizon one may extend the observed path constantly after H as a data encoding, not as an assertion about the physical process's unobserved future. However, the predictive state is a probability law on a path space. The cited theorem supplies neither finite-dimensional mass-action coordinates nor all finite chemical realizations of that law. Minimizing predictive information would still not enumerate nonminimal hidden extensions or identify hidden-only reactions. Markovization alone therefore does not close the requested fibre.

Lindquist, Mitter and Picci's nonlinear realization paper assumes, in Section 2, a centered, mean-square-continuous, purely nondeterministic stationary process on the whole real time axis, together with a Wiener innovation representation. Theorem 1 addresses minimal states within its chaos/splitting-space framework. Section 8 explicitly treats the development as structural rather than algorithmic and notes the nontrivial innovation-representation requirement. [Official primary PDF](https://mitter.lids.mit.edu/publications/32_toward_a_theory_LNCIS.pdf); [author-uploaded primary text used to inspect Sections 2 and 8 and Theorem 1](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/37592599_Toward_a_theory_of_nonlinear_stochastic_realization).

**Failed hypotheses.** A deterministic fixed start followed by a nondegenerate diffusion law is not stationary. Passing to equilibrium or a two-sided stationary version changes the experiment. No Wiener-innovation representation satisfying that theorem's assumptions has been established for the admitted general stopped projection. Thus this specific realization theorem cannot be imported unchanged. The official PDF was retrieved but its scan was not visually inspected; the section check used the identified author-upload text. A later Taylor–Pavon realization paper was accessible only at abstract level and supplies no theorem-level negative conclusion in this audit.

## 4. Finite observable-operator rank: a concrete failed hypothesis

Wu and Noe's OOM definition, equation (1), factors word probabilities through an m-dimensional linear state. Equation (6) is the past/future feature matrix C_12. Section 3.2, Assumption 2, explicitly assumes an m-dimensional OOM and an asymptotic stationarity condition; Assumptions 1 and 3 impose data-limit and rank conditions. Theorem 1 is conditional on all three. The continuous-observation Theorem 3 retains them, adding a closed Euclidean observation space and bounded features. [Primary 2016 conference paper, Sections 2.2–4.2 inspected](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2016/file/296472c9542ad4d4788d543508116cbc-Paper.pdf).

The relevant rank is linear predictive/Hankel rank, not number of chemical species. The following exact test uses the same adjacent-observation feature block as equation (6), with feature length L=1. It does not replace the continuous diffusion by a finite-state jump chain or coarse-grain the observation.

### Proposition: a one-reaction stopped diffusion has infinite observable two-time rank

Take the single reaction A -> 2A with rate 1. Fix x0>0 and I=(l,r) with 0<l<x0<r<infinity. Let

    dX_t = X_t dt + sqrt(X_t) dW_t,
    tau = first exit from I,
    Z_t = X_(t wedge tau).

The record is held at the reached endpoint. Fix any Delta>0 with 2 Delta<=H. For f,g in C_c^infinity(I), extended by zero to the endpoints, define the observed bilinear form

    B_Delta(f,g) = E_x0[f(Z_Delta) g(Z_(2 Delta))].

For every integer N>=1 there exist f_1,...,f_N and g_1,...,g_N of this class such that the N by N matrix [B_Delta(f_i,g_j)] is nonsingular. Consequently no exact finite-dimensional OOM representation of the sampled observed law can factor all these feature matrices.

**Proof.** All coefficients are smooth and uniformly elliptic on the closed interval. Write K_t for the Dirichlet killed semigroup on I, and k_t(x,y) for its interior density. The standard regular-interval killed-diffusion facts used in the previously reviewed two-time proof give continuity and strict positivity of k_t for t>0 and x,y in I. The generator is

    Lf = x f' + (x/2) f''.

For a direct specification of its self-adjoint realization, put

    m(x) = 2 exp(2x)/x,          p(x) = exp(2x).

Then Lf = m^(-1)(p f')'. The Dirichlet form

    E(f,g) = integral_I p(x) f'(x) g'(x) dx,
    domain(E) = H_0^1(I)

on L^2(I,m dx) is closed; m and p are bounded above and below by positive constants. Its nonpositive self-adjoint generator has domain H^2(I) intersect H_0^1(I) and the displayed expression. Its semigroup is K_t by uniqueness of the regular Dirichlet problem. In particular K_Delta is injective: if K_Delta g=0, the spectral theorem gives

    0 = ||K_Delta g||^2 = integral_(-infinity,0] exp(2 Delta lambda) dmu_g(lambda).

The integrand is strictly positive at every finite lambda, so mu_g=0 and g=0. Zero as a possible spectral accumulation point of K_Delta creates no kernel.

Let h(x)=k_Delta(x0,x)>0. The full stopped Markov property gives

    B_Delta(f,g) = integral_I h(x) f(x) (K_Delta g)(x) dx.       (A)

This is not survival-conditioned data. If absorption has occurred by the first time, f vanishes; if it occurs between the two times, g vanishes. Equation (A) is therefore an observable cylinder expectation of the actual held record, with exactly the required killing restriction and no extra exit indicator supplied as data.

Choose any N linearly independent g_j in C_c^infinity(I). Suppose a linear combination of the functionals f -> B_Delta(f,g_j) vanishes for every f in that test space. Equation (A) and distributional testing imply

    h K_Delta(sum_j c_j g_j) = 0  almost everywhere on I.

Since h>0, injectivity implies sum_j c_j g_j=0; independence gives every c_j=0. Thus the N functionals are linearly independent. The evaluation map f -> (B_Delta(f,g_1),...,B_Delta(f,g_N)) has range R^N: otherwise a nonzero linear functional annihilating its proper range would give the dependence just excluded. Choose f_i whose image vectors are the standard basis. The pairing matrix is then the identity. QED.

The density and regular Dirichlet operator providers are the same ones specified in [the reviewed two-time manuscript, Sections 3–5](TWO-TIME-SAMPLED-EXTENSION.md). The source history remains classical scalar diffusion theory, including [Kent's Theorem 8.1 and interval boundary framework](https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~sschmid/Courses/Stat376/Papers/Langevin/KentAdvAppProb1978.pdf). The proposition is an author hand diagnostic, not a new general spectral theorem.

### Exact connection to the cited observable feature matrix

Set the first two sampled observations to Z_Delta and Z_(2 Delta), and take phi_1=(f_i) and phi_2=(g_j). Their feature matrix C_12 is precisely the matrix in the proposition. If an m-dimensional OOM represented this law, integrating its word factorization against f_i and g_j would yield

    C_12(i,j) = [omega Xi(f_i)] [Xi(g_j) sigma],

and therefore rank(C_12)<=m for every feature choice. Taking N=m+1 contradicts the proposition. Boundary atoms cause no escape: the features vanish there; even granting an operator-valued-measure extension accommodating the mixed boundary/interior law, this finite-dimensional factorization has the same rank bound. Thus the failure is tied to the actual feature block, not to an unrelated operator on hidden states.

This one-species example is a legitimate subclass diagnostic: finite species and a finite reaction list do not imply the finite predictive rank required by this method. It is **not** a negative result about a finite-dimensional nonlinear state, finite parameterization, or a target-dependent finite identifying signature. This very process has a one-dimensional chemical realization, and the separate scalar adapter proves finite identifying signatures within its declared source class. Approximate low-rank models and coarsened observations are not excluded; they answer different questions from exact observational equivalence.

## 5. What the attack establishes, and the exact remaining bridge

Three tempting replacements for the missing theorem have now been checked rather than assumed:

1. A structural bisimulation/homomorphism gives a sufficient comparison, but the inspected theorem does not make it necessary for the fixed-start trace law of our admitted chemical class.
2. Predictive Markovization retains nonlocal path information, but does not identify every finite mass-action realization of the predictive law.
3. Exact finite-linear-rank realization cannot cover the whole admitted source class merely because each source is finite. The proposition disproves that particular hypothesis transfer without disproving nonlinear or finite-signature approaches.

The still-needed result is a stop-faithful, fixed-start, all-rival completeness theorem connecting observed path laws to the entire admitted physical reaction-network fibre, with its unavoidable full-generator equivalences. It must either justify a complete nonlocal signature or classify all compatible finite mass-action realizations without presupposing their hidden size. Hidden-only reactions cannot be removed merely because they have zero instantaneous projected covariance weight: they can affect later hidden coupling or the full-state exit clock.

No inspected provider supplies that bridge. This is a bounded conclusion about the named sources and their exact hypotheses, not a universal absence theorem and not a proof that the master problem is impossible. No further initial-jet component, stronger preparation experiment, changed stopping rule, or new runtime evidence is substituted for it.

# Literal opened drawings and source-cycle curves

Six independently reviewed modules derive geometric preparation from actual edge curves. They preserve all 47 preceding owned sources and 41 providers.

## Actual opened drawing

Each new hybrid-parent tip is the midpoint of its original incoming edge arc. Its new pendant edge follows the first half of that arc. Skeleton vertices and edges retain their original drawing. Original point/arc injectivity and incidence conditions derive the full crossing-free drawing of the literal opened graph, preserving parallel edge occurrences. Undirected occurrence walks traverse original edges forwards or backwards. Their vertex sets, edge sets and simplicity predicates are combinatorial. The physical trace is exactly the union of the traversed original arcs and the initial vertex; injectivity of a nonempty vertex-simple walk is derived from original incidence conditions.

Two nonempty simple occurrence walks with the same endpoints, disjoint edge sets and no shared internal vertices therefore give a continuous injective map from AddCircle(1) onto their physical union. documents.body:
# A fixed-start scalar derivative adapter to the prior positive-moment certificate

Author: dot (OpenAI). 22 October 2026 UTC.

Status: complete author hand argument with scoped coordinating hand-review PASS on 22 October 2026; see the separate SCALAR-ADAPTER-COORDINATING-REVIEW.md receipt. No execution, Lean verification, or historical novelty claim. The positive atomic moment theorem is inherited; the experiment-specific work below is the stopped scalar law-to-derivative adapter and the return to the correct reaction-law target.

## 1. Precise scope and target

Fix x0>0, a bounded open interval I containing x0 with closure contained in (0,infinity), and H>0. Admit any nonempty finite scalar mass-action reaction list

    n A -> (n+v) A,   n>=0, v an integer, v!=0, n+v>=0,

with positive active rates kappa_(n,v). Repeated identical edges, if allowed, are aggregated. The target and every rival use the same x0, I and H. There is no source-degree bound, no rival-size bound, no change of preparation, and no extra species. Null reactions are excluded because they are invisible to the diffusion.

Write

    b(x)=sum_n beta_n x^n,   beta_n=sum_v v*kappa_(n,v),
    a(x)=sum_n alpha_n x^n,  alpha_n=sum_v v^2*kappa_(n,v).

The variance coefficients alpha_n are nonnegative, with finite nonempty support S. Moreover beta_n=0 whenever alpha_n=0. Let r=|S| for the target. This counts active reactant degrees, not reaction edges or total polynomial degree.

The observation is the exact law on C([0,H],R) of the scalar diffusion

    dX=b(X)dt+sqrt(a(X))dW,

stopped at tau=inf{t: X_t not in I} and held afterwards. Since a>0 on the positive axis, all coefficients are smooth and uniformly nondegenerate on the closure of I; the localized law is unique. The stop is observable from X. This is the autonomous scalar class used in the finite-initial-jet obstruction, enlarged from unit births to general admitted scalar jumps. It is not the general unreconstructed-hidden-species class.

The primary target is the diffusion-law equivalence class, namely all reaction lists with the same alpha_n and beta_n. General reaction edges and individual rates cannot be recovered from these two sums without an additional admitted-family uniqueness statement.

## 2. Law-to-derivative adapter at the one fixed start

**Lemma 1.** The exact stopped law determines every finite collection of numbers

    a^(j)(x0), b^(j)(x0),  j>=0.

This is a statement about deterministic invariants of a probability law, not a consistent finite-sample estimator or differentiation of the drift of a single noisy path.

**Proof.** Work in the completed natural filtration of the canonical stopped process. It has the unique continuous semimartingale decomposition

    X_t=x0+D_t+M_t,
    D_t=integral_0^t 1_(s<tau) b(X_s) ds,
    [X]_t=integral_0^t 1_(s<tau) a(X_s) ds.

Bounded coefficients on the stopped compact interval justify the martingale identities in the natural filtration by conditioning. Uniqueness follows because a continuous local martingale of finite variation is constant. Quadratic variation is likewise unique. Thus the law determines D and [X], up to the usual indistinguishability of canonical versions.

Before tau, take the time densities U0=a(X) and V0=b(X). At zero use right limits. At tau use the continuous left limit, then hold this value, rather than replacing it by the post-exit zero density. These are continuous semimartingales because they equal the smooth functions a(X^stop) and b(X^stop). The density construction is possible for each finite collection using common almost-sure subsequences for quadratic-variation approximations and continuity. No claim that a fixed universal subsequence works simultaneously for every possible source is needed for the identification implication.

If Uj=a^(j)(X^stop), Ito's cross-variation formula gives

    d[X,Uj]_t/dt = 1_(t<tau) a(X_t) a^(j+1)(X_t).

Divide by the strictly positive U0 before the stop, then extend continuously to the stop and hold. This recovers U_(j+1). The same recursion with Vj=b^(j)(X^stop) recovers V_(j+1):

    U_(j+1) = (d[X,Uj]/dt)/U0,
    V_(j+1) = (d[X,Vj]/dt)/U0,                 t<tau.

The initial values are the claimed derivatives. Since tau>0 almost surely, every finite recursion is defined on an initial positive time interval. Values after tau are never mistaken for the physical coefficient. Alternatively, equality of two laws gives common canonical D and [X], then the same finite recursion under that common law proves equality of all these deterministic initial values. QED.

The variance side is path-functional quadratic-variation extraction. The drift side uses the exact law's canonical drift, not a pathwise drift estimator. This distinction matters when counting physical information.

## 3. Exact supplying theorem and normalization

Let E be the shifted Euler operator

    (E f)(x)=f(x)+x f'(x).

It satisfies E^k(x^n)=(n+1)^k x^n. Define the law invariants

    M_k=(E^k a)(x0)=sum_n alpha_n x0^n (n+1)^k,
    B_k=(E^k b)(x0)=sum_n beta_n x0^n (n+1)^k.

For each k these require derivatives only through order k, so Lemma 1 supplies them without changing the initial state. In particular M_0=a(x0)>0. The actual normalized positive atomic law is

    mu=sum_(n in S) [alpha_n x0^n / M_0] delta_(n+1).

Its r nodes are distinct and strictly positive, including when the zero-order reactant n=0 is admitted. Its weights are strictly positive and sum to one. Its ordinary moments are M_k/M_0. A rival produces the same kind of finite positive law, with no bound on its support size or maximum node.

The relevant previously checked project declaration is

    Astra.CommonMoment.support_card_le_of_equal_sparse_moments

from CMSeparation.lean, reproduced with exact source and verification scope in the [CM-T02 component certificate](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/514648b697aeed8f46582109cfeefcd7707cd738/research/2026-10-15-common-moment-checked-component/CM-T02-CERTIFICATE-001.json). It assumes two finite strictly positive probability laws on distinct strictly positive real nodes and 2*target.card+1 distinct natural-number exponents with equal moments. Its conclusion is rival.card<=target.card. The direction is important. It does not by its stated conclusion alone identify the nodes, original reaction list, or physical observation adapter.

Here ordinary exponents 0,...,2r allow the classical stronger support certificate directly: for the target nodes z_1,...,z_r, put

    Q(z)=product_(i=1)^r (z-z_i)^2.

This degree-2r polynomial is nonnegative everywhere and zero exactly at the target nodes. Equal moments through 2r imply integral Q dnu=integral Q dmu=0. Positive rival weights force every rival node into the target set. The first r moment equations then identify the weights by the ordinary Vandermonde matrix. Thus nu=mu.

This annihilating-square proof is classical and is the ordinary-moment specialization of the existing positive-support mechanism. Neither it nor its 2r+1 count is a new contribution of this note. The source-normalization step, node shift, and physical derivative adapter are stated explicitly to prevent importing the supplier without its hypotheses. The old abstract component's Lean evidence does not verify this new stochastic adapter.

## 4. All-rival finite signature for the scalar law fibre

**Theorem 2.** Fix any target in Section 1 with r active reactant degrees. For every admitted finite rival, regardless of its degree or edge count, the following are equivalent:

1. The exact stopped path laws from the common x0 on [0,H] are equal.
2. Their finite signatures agree:

       M_k,  k=0,...,2r;     B_k,  k=0,...,r-1.

3. All variance and drift coefficients agree: alpha_n=alpha'_n and beta_n=beta'_n for every n.

This uses 3r+1 scalar law invariants, not 3r+1 trajectories, sampling times, preparations, or finite-sample measurements.

**Proof.** (1) implies (2) by Lemma 1. Suppose (2). The equality of M_0 supplies the same positive normalization. Section 3's positive-moment certificate gives equality of the normalized measures, hence identical supports S and identical alpha_n x0^n. Since x0>0, alpha_n=alpha'_n. In particular the rival has no hidden additional reactant degree: positivity of its variance coefficients is essential to this conclusion.

The supports of both drift polynomials lie in the now-common S. The r equations for B_k give

    sum_(n in S) (beta_n-beta'_n) x0^n (n+1)^k=0,
                                                    k=0,...,r-1.

The Vandermonde matrix at distinct nodes n+1 is invertible; beta_n=beta'_n for every n. This proves (3). Finally (3) gives the same scalar coefficients and the same observable stop, so localized uniqueness gives (1). QED.

**Unit-birth specialization.** If the source class consists only of nA->(n+1)A, then b=a. The signature M_0,...,M_(2r) alone is sufficient. Every coefficient is an individual aggregated reaction rate, so this identifies the exact graph and rates against all finite unit-birth rivals. This is the same source class and observable-stop experiment as the preceding finite-initial-jet obstruction. There is no contradiction: that obstruction lets r grow with the prescribed jet order, whereas this count depends on the fixed target's r.

**Unit forward/reverse specialization.** If only v=+1 and v=-1 are allowed, with v=-1 excluded when n=0, the identified coefficients recover the rates as kappa_(n,+1)=(alpha_n+beta_n)/2 and kappa_(n,-1)=(alpha_n-beta_n)/2. Admission already guarantees these rates are nonnegative and the excluded n=0 reverse rate is zero.

**General jumps.** Network/rate uniqueness is false without such restrictions. At reactant degree n=1, allow jumps v=1,2,3. Positive rate vectors (1,4,1) and (4,1,2) both give beta_1=12 and alpha_1=26. They therefore have exactly the same observed diffusion law under the theorem, although the individual rates differ. This is the familiar generator-level ambiguity, not a new nonidentification mechanism.

## 5. What is and is not resolved

The exact result combines an experiment-specific fixed-start derivative adapter with the existing positive-moment supplier. It does not rename a full-state coefficient/cone criterion as a new theorem. Faul, Hoessly and Xia's [generator and reaction-vector analysis](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0956792526100382) remains the prior structural background; the coefficient sums above are its scalar specialization.

The result needs an autonomous scalar observed diffusion and an observable interval exit. For a general projected hidden diffusion, the observed drift is a conditional characteristic rather than the unconditioned polynomial b(X), and the variation density can depend on hidden state. The recursion then follows full-state covariance directions, not ordinary derivatives in the observed coordinate. No positive atomic degree response follows automatically. The finite-family neutral and catalytic reconstructions supply special closures, not a uniform closure for all finite hidden reaction networks.

If r is unknown, the theorem is target-dependent existence of a finite signature. It does not by itself supply a finite-precision stopping rule or an effective representation of exact law access. An adaptive Hankel/positive-support decision procedure would need an explicitly admitted exact-arithmetic response oracle. There is no stability, statistical sample-complexity, noisy-data, discrete-time, or arbitrary hidden-stop conclusion.

In particular, a finite list of law-determined real invariants is not automatically an effective legal finite-experiment or response interface. The proof supplies no implementation of exact canonical-drift extraction or exact derivative queries from an external representation of a law.

Historical novelty of the fixed-start adapter or its combined scalar statement is not established. All bracket, canonical semimartingale, positive-moment and Vandermonde ingredients are classical; only the displayed experiment-specific join is being recorded here as an author-checked specialization. General fixed-start partial-observation closure and a full formal stochastic proof remain open.
