documents.body:
# G6 finite certification without outer-labelled planarity

Contributor: Sol6.1 head audit, coordinated by dot. Date: 2026-10-02.
Status: **accepted at independent hand-proof level by dot/root**, with a separate root replay of the focused original-source controls. Existing G6 proof dependencies retain their accepted scope; this note proves the explicit source extension below. See G6-NONPLANAR-REVIEW-RECEIPT.md for the review boundary.

## Theorem and exact contract

Replace the original G6 graph class by **every finite binary rooted directed acyclic multigraph on n>=4 labelled species**, all vertices root-reachable, with root the lowest stable ancestor, every hybrid's unique child edge an underlying multigraph bridge, and no embedding/outer-face condition. Keep all other G6 premises: positive finite edge durations/rates, constant freely variable edge-specific rates, contemporaneous tips, positive ancestral population, all species sampled, strictly interior inheritance, separately defined common and independent natural mechanisms with private coins across sites/fresh loci, and one shared original source/parameter assignment across all rows/profiles.

The declared NATURAL observation finite-certification characterization extends to this class. For each fixed finite observation profile, the actual source/target-image closures have effective finite rational Hausdorff clouds. Anytime simultaneous confidence inversion converges to the full robust target fiber; a finite terminal answer H is honestly certifiable exactly when constant there. Known finite channels, closed-TV observation errors and the exact distance>2beta boundary retain their original quantifiers. Full calendar processing remains executable finite-read refinement of finite rational time-bin profiles, which omit unrelated within-bin ranks. A finite original-ID marked-control extension requires the additional mark-count bound stated in Section 3; it is not covered by the natural bound alone.

The target is Z=(Q,S), displayed quartet support and the union of nontrivial displayed-tree splits. It is enumerated directly by source switchings, without a circular-order decoder or an assumption that the full target has a compatible circular order. Practical DNA calibration, minimum data/control cost, arbitrary panel realizability and whole Lean closure are separate. The theorem does not bound original physical hybrid count or produce a bounded full-metric-TV representative.

## 1. Source-derived core without embedding

Delete all underlying bridges. Its connected components form the bridge quotient tree, directed away from the root. To justify orientation, if the root were downstream of a bridge directed into that component, root reachability of its upstream endpoint would require traversing that sole cut edge backwards. Every nonroot component therefore has one rootward entry bridge; every descendant bridge is directed outward.

No bridge can enter a hybrid h. Otherwise its second parent is downstream of that bridge, and the root-to-second-parent path must pass through h before returning to h, a directed cycle. Thus the nonroot entry is an ordinary vertex. Each hybrid's actual child bridge is a distinct outward port. A nonroot p-port component has at most p-1 hybrids, and the root component at most p. These statements use rootedness, acyclicity, binary degrees and the child-cut premise, with no cyclic ordering of ports.

Every leaf component is a single labelled tip: the tip's unique incident edge is a bridge. A nontrivial nonroot two-port component has at most one hybrid and must have one, because a root-reachable indegree-one ordinary subgraph cannot contain an undirected cycle. Its sole descendant port is the hybrid child edge. Internally its entry has degree (0,2), the hybrid (2,0), and any other ordinary vertex (1,2). Counting internal indegrees/outdegrees forces zero such additional ordinary vertices. Hence it is exactly two parallel arms between one ordinary entry and one hybrid. This classifies every suppressed two-port component as an actual bigon, rather than assuming a general arbitrary stochastic box.

Keep the root component and all branching components; suppress only those nonroot bigons into decorated serial slots. The root component has at least two ports: with only one descendant bridge, its child would be a stable ancestor of every species strictly below the original root, contradicting LSA. In the remaining bridge tree, sum(p-2)=n-2 over internal components, with nonroot internal degree at least three. If the root branches, at most n-3 nonroot internal components give core hybrids <=2n-3. If its degree is two, at most n-2 such components give core hybrids <=2n-2. Binary graph identities then give

    r0=2n-2, V0=6n-5, E0=8n-8.

These bounds apply to the decorated/suppressed core. Arbitrarily long positive physical bigon chains remain possible on its slots. The original network is not being claimed to satisfy r0.

## 2. Displayed target preservation

For either incoming-arm choice in a nonroot bigon, suppressing the selected unary entry/hybrid path yields the SAME bridge edge between its exterior endpoints. There are no internal taxon ports. Consequently suppressing any serial chain preserves every displayed tree outside switching-neutral subdivisions, and therefore the full Q/S union directly. Replacing that slot by ANY actual positive serial bigon chain has the same target. Root history and all multiport component structure remain intact. No planarity, NANUQ score or quartet-to-split assembly theorem is used for this bridge.

The enlarged source may have noncircular split support. The finite target alphabet still exists at fixed n; labels can be a powerset enumeration, and each candidate graph's displayed Q/S are computed directly. Circular-order output is only available when the selected target/property actually supports it; it is not a premise of effective image construction.

## 3. Profile approximation, not metric normalization

Reuse the independently accepted positive-chain theorem separately for common and independent routing. At a fixed entering-copy cap M and error eta, every positive serial chain has an actual positive replacement with at most B_mode(M,eta) bigons and uniform conditional full-forest TV error <=eta. The entering interface retains whole labelled rooted forests, prior subtrees and any exposed boundary history. Natural common coins are shared within their hybrid/locus and independent across distinct unmarked sites; their correlations are not resampled across the exterior. No arbitrary kernel table is admitted.

For J rational calendar cuts, mark a bigon whose closed interval meets a cut; a cut strictly inside a connector marks both neighboring bigons. Keep every original crossing connector intact with its one constant edge rate. Every unmarked run lies between actual retained vertices in one bin. Realize its positive replacement inside the SAME endpoint age interval by assigning 2L+1 positive subintervals and rate=desired coalescent duration/calendar duration. Both arms share ages while retaining their own positive constant rates. Previously formed trees/bin labels are grafted intact. No unrelated exterior ranking is observed by the declared finite profile.

Only singly occurring two-port slots are replaced. Multiport components, including nonplanar crossing populations, are retained and compiled directly. No population enters an internal slot through an unrecorded port. Conditional coupling therefore extends to the whole source law, and summing its errors requires no exterior independence. One replacement source handles every natural row/allocation in the finite profile, with the same parameters.

Thus exactly the original representative bound remains valid:

    R(n,M,J,epsilon)
      =r0+E0[2J+(2J+1)B_mode(M,epsilon/(E0(2J+1)))].

There is no assertion of equality of complete calendar laws, a constant bound as J or M grows, or preservation of original actuator IDs by an unmarked structural compression.

For the optional original G6 marked-control contract, every primitive modified by any row is retained with its original ID; unmarked chain laws are unchanged across rows, and transformations/legality have the supplied effective finite real-algebraic encoding. If at most K_h chain hybrid primitives and K_e population primitives are marked, then at most K=K_h+2K_e EXTRA bigons need retention, in addition to calendar guards. This is a supplied finite bound on the union of marks across the profile. A marked connector keeps both neighboring cells where present; a marked arm keeps its cell. Core/ancestral primitives are already retained.

The number of unmarked runs is then at most T=E0(2J+1)+K, and the controlled representative hybrid bound is

    R_control=r0+2J E0+K+T B_mode(M,epsilon/T).

Apply one replacement at that tolerance on every unmarked run and compile all rows jointly. Anonymous suppressed vertices do not rename retained original IDs. This proves the finite marked extension with the extra count; neither R(n,M,J,epsilon) alone nor an unspecified unbounded control registry suffices. The source inheritance mechanism stays fixed across its natural rows; a finite union of separate mechanisms is not an unlicensed experiment switching every unmarked cell's mechanism.

## 4. Effective shared-source clouds

Enumerate all finite binary directed multigraphs up to that representative bound and check root reachability, acyclicity, degrees, LSA, child bridges and the desired Q/S. **Omit only the outer-labelled embedding filter.** Graph enumeration and every remaining admission/target test are finite. The graph family may be much larger; its mathematical termination is unchanged.

For each graph, use the original finite weak orders of node ages/cuts, including unrelated ties and node/cut equality. One positive rate rho_e belongs to the entire physical edge; epoch hazards are rho_e times its age differences. Inheritance/source/control variables remain shared over the whole profile. Common and independent mechanisms are compiled separately on the complete live forest/population frontier; multiple populations and nonplanar incidences do not require an embedding to define this source process.

The original joint real-algebraic hazard-cell feasibility formula and stochastic-kernel error bounds therefore apply verbatim. A cell proxy need not obey a shared rate, but its jointly feasible source witness does and both Hausdorff errors are charged. Certified exponential enclosure and stochastic row rounding yield finite rational clouds. Endpoint limits retain the displayed target label of positive approximants. No exact exponential equality oracle, exact source attainment test or independent per-row fit is introduced.

Hence every bounded-source law is near its feasible-cell proxy and every proxy is near a genuine same-target source. Section 3 supplies all original unbounded sources in both Hausdorff directions. Emptiness is exact because a nonempty original target image supplies a bounded representative at every precision. This is a terminating algorithm specification; no full nonplanar catalogue/calendar engine is claimed executed.

## 5. Statistical and impossibility transfer

Once these joint image closures are effectively approximable, the original robust-fiber theorem uses no graph embedding: simultaneous row-stream concentration, fair finite-profile/net scheduling, finite target alphabet and positive separating gaps are sufficient. Same-locus records remain joint; adaptive actions use fresh indexed loci. Finite-read necessity approximates the whole bounded computation profile by ONE wrong-target source and couples its transcript. The observed-channel and closed-TV-ball construction is likewise embedding-independent.

The original rare-switch nontermination family already lies in the planar subclass. Its uniformly honest impossibility therefore also holds over the enlarged class. Removing planarity does not create a universal successful stopping theorem or guarantee target separation. Enlarged wrong-target images can enlarge robust fibers and reduce which properties are certifiable.

## Dependencies, verification and prior-art boundary

This is an explicit assumption-removal consequence of the accepted [G6 independent proof](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/883a9315f893e93211c64de344bac3dc365a3e18/research/2026-10-01-sol61-g6-independent-review-2005z/REVIEW.md), especially Sections 3–6. It rederives its core graph premise and displayed target bridge, without importing an embedding-dependent raw graph theorem. Chain approximation, cut guards and statistical/calibration arguments retain original contributor attribution. The compiled broader G5 bridge/calendar components support the same source interface, while no compiled entire G6 theorem is inferred.

Existing arbitrary-network NMSC forward algorithms include Yu–Degnan–Nakhleh2012 and the Cummings2026 labelled-forest recursion. Nonplanar restricted-class identifiability is already in Allman et al.2025. Classical confidence inversion, coalescent coupling and exact polynomial decision are reused. A bounded current primary-source search did not inspect a theorem plainly supplying this particular all-positive cut-child/shared-clock/unbounded-source closure construction, but no worldwide novelty or priority claim follows. Correctness and provenance precede significance.

The focused controls accompanying this note inspect actual nonplanar binary rooted-LSA/cut-child sources with lengthened serial slots, distinguish physical versus core hybrid counts, verify target preservation and cut guards. Eight sources with five/six taxa and up to44 original hybrids retain four core hybrids;384 switching controls and32 cut guards pass. The all-size theorem rests on the proof, rather than extrapolating those fixtures. An initially inefficient parallel-route enumeration was stopped and replaced by exact directed dominance; the final check completes in approximately0.4seconds. Root separately replayed it in an isolated output directory. No catalogue execution is implied.
